articleTitle: Tutorial on Raman and Cladding-Pumped Fiber Amplifiers and Lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Due to its versatility, Raman amplification is certain to play an ever increasing role in optical communication systems. In this tutorial, we will review the fundamentals of Raman amplification in optical fibers. The issues of conversion efficiency, noise, and pump sources will be discussed. The evolution of Raman amplifiers, discrete and distributed, and recent experimental results will be described.

articleTitle: Measurement techniques for high-speed WDM systems experiments
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. The recent explosive growth of fiber transmission capacity in laboratories around the world is the result of various new experimental techniques. These measurement techniques will be described and, in particular, techniques that lead to misleading experimental results will be scrutinized.

articleTitle: Hierarchical optical path cross-connect systems for large scale WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Hierarchical optical path architecture consisting of wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) bands and channels are suitable for large-scale WDM backbone networks. A hierarchical optical path crossconnect system (OPXC) using a matrix WDM scheme is proposed as a reliable and economical high-performance node architecture.

articleTitle: Transparent vs. opaque vs. translucent wavelength-routed optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This study evaluates the relative merits of three approaches (transparency, opacity, and translucency) for establishing calls in a wavelength-routed optical network. Call-admission algorithms employ online bit-error-rate computation and include the effects of transmission impairments.

articleTitle: Measurement of the maximum speed of PMD fluctuation in installed field fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) transient recorder setup was realized enabling for the first time to our knowledge the monitoring of fast PMD fluctuation with a bandwidth of up to 1 MHz. Thirty-six hours of observation of an installed field fiber exhibits significant PMD variation within 10 ms.

articleTitle: Limitation of optical first-order PMD compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new theoretical model exhibits that first-order polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) compensation extends the maximum acceptable PMD to 0.35 times the bit period T. At 10 gbit/s chromatic dispersion of 850 ps/nm (50 km SMF) reduces this PMD limit to 0.29 T.

articleTitle: A simple dynamic polarization mode dispersion compensator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We experimentally validate at 10 Gbit/s a new and simple polarization-mode dispersion compensator based on the dynamic maximization of the degree of polarization. First-order compensation is demonstrated and ultimate statistical performance is numerically assessed.

articleTitle: Fast restoration in a mesh network of optical cross-connects
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed restoration method for mesh networks of optical cross-connects (OXCs) that is competitive with SONET ring restoration speeds. This approach is especially adapted to OXCs with optic fabrics where electronic signal performance or fault detection is available only at add/drop ports.

articleTitle: A new scheduling algorithm for asynchronous variable length IP traffic incorporating void filling
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate that optimum switch performance can be achieved by matching the basic delay line unit in the optical buffer to the degree of self-similarity of the input traffic, in tandem with a scheduling algorithm for void filling.

articleTitle: 100 nm bandwidth flat gain Raman amplifiers pumped and gain-equalized by 12-wavelength-channel WDM high power laser diodes
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate 100 nm bandwidth Raman amplifiers using 12-wavelength-channel WDM pump laser diode unit. The gain flatness is less than /spl plusmn/0.5 dB, which is achieved through an asymmetric channel allocation of pump and without any gain equalization filters.

articleTitle: Polarization-mode dispersion impairment in return-to-zero and nonreturn-to-zero systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Using 10-Gbit/s signals, amplitude modulated with either a return-to-zero (RZ) or a nonreturn-to-zero format (NRZ), we measured optically preamplified receiver sensitivity after distortion by polarization-made dispersion (PMD). RZ modulation was found to be more resilient to PMD than NRZ modulation.

articleTitle: 3 Tbit/s (160 Gbit/s/spl times/19 ch) OTDM/WDM transmission experiment
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 3 Tbit/s (160 Gbit/s/spl times/19 channels) optical signal is successfully transmitted over 40 km dispersion-shifted fiber. Low noise supercontinuum signal pulse sources and 70 nm bandwidth tellurite-based optical amplifiers are used for 3 Tbit/s signal generation and amplification.

articleTitle: Long term field demonstration of optical PMD compensation on an installed OC-192 link
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate the world's first long term optical PMD compensation for an OC-192 (9.95328 Gb/s SONET) signal on the installed fiber infrastructure of a network operator in East Texas. With a line PMD of 30 ps, BER improvement greater than 4 orders of magnitude has been achieved.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental studies of the influence of the number of crosstalk signals on the penalty caused by incoherent optical crosstalk
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Calculations based on the exact probability density function of the received power show that for a fixed total crosstalk power, the incoherent crosstalk penalty increases with the number of crosstalk signals. Performed experiments verify this.

articleTitle: Narrow band 1.02 Tbit/s (51/spl times/20 Gbit/s) soliton DWDM transmission over 1000 km of standard fiber with 100 km amplifier spans
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 1.02 Tbit/s (51-wavelength each at 20 Gbit/s) dense WDM (0.4 nm channel-spacing) soliton transmission over 1000 km of standard step-index fiber with 100 lan (21 dB loss) amplifier spans was successfully achieved for the first time.

articleTitle: Automatic polarization-mode dispersion compensation in 40-Gbit/s transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We believe we demonstrated automatic polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) compensation in 40-Gbit/s NRZ transmission for the first time. By the feedback control of an optical PMD compensator to maximize the 20-GHz intensity of received baseband signals, we more than doubled the allowable PMD from 11 to 23 ps.

articleTitle: An all-pass filter dispersion compensator using planar waveguide ring resonators
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A compact, multichannel dispersion-compensating filter is demonstrated with D=/spl plusmn/4200 ps/nm, a /spl plusmn/5 ps group delay ripple, low loss, a 4.5-GHz passband, and the design to compensate for higher-order dispersion.

articleTitle: 640 Gb/s transmission of sixty-four 10 Gb/s WDM channels over 7200 km with 0.33 (bits/s)/Hz spectral efficiency
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Sixty-four 10 gb/s WDM channels were transmitted over 7200 km is a spectral bandwidth of 15.1 nm for a spectral efficiency of 0.33 (bits/s)Hz. Error free operation was achieved for all channels.

articleTitle: Comparison of four-wave mixing and cross phase modulation penalties in dense WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The relative impact of four-wave mixing (FWM) and cross phase modulation (XPM) is investigated by treating them as noiselike impairments. We show that XPM affects wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission more strongly than FWM for the range of fiber parameters investigated.

articleTitle: Concatenated FEC experiment over 5000 km long straight line WDM test bed
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A concatenated forward error correction (FEC) code yielded 10-dB coding gain in a straight line laboratory experiment over a 5000-km optically amplified test bed. We used this margin to reduce power per channel, and thus nonlinearities, allowing us to demonstrate channel spacings as close as 0.13 nm for 2.5 Gbit/s transmission.

articleTitle: Design and manufacture of dispersion compensating fibre for simultaneous compensation of dispersion and dispersion slope
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The negative dispersion slope of dispersion-compensating fibers has been optimized by increasing the width of the depressed cladding. Simultaneous compensation and dispersion slope has been demonstrated on an actual link.

articleTitle: Radio-over-fiber distribution using an optical millimeter-wave/DWDM overlay
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate an optical MM-wave/DWDM overlay using optical suppressed-carrier modulation to simultaneously upconvert multi-wavelength subcarriers to 35 GHz. Performance of the system is analyzed for radio-over-fiber distribution.

articleTitle: Electrically tunable power efficient dispersion compensating fiber Bragg gratings for dynamic operation in nonlinear lightwave systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a power efficient (<0.5 W) tunable dispersion compensating fiber Bragg grating device and show for the first time dynamic optimization of dispersion in a nonlinear lightwave system. Operation is demonstrated in a 20 Gbit/s single channel NRZ system where the device was used to adjust the dispersion to the power-dependent optimal dispersion required for optimum performance.

articleTitle: High-speed 32-channel optical wavelength selector using PLC hybrid integration
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have developed a new high-speed 32-channel optical wavelength selector (OWS) with gate drivers using PLC hybrid integration. It has excellent characteristics consisting of a low insertion loss of 2.3 dB, a low cross talk of -46 dB and the error-free optical wavelength selection of 10-Gbit/s optical signal.

articleTitle: Broadband Raman amplifiers in the spectral range of 1480-1620 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Raman amplifiers using germano-silica fibers are demonstrated with a continuous operation bandwidth from 20 nm to more than 100 nm, 20-40 dB net gain and 4.5-7 dB noise figure. Single-, dual-, and triple-wavelength pumping are implemented in the configuration incorporating circulators for pump/signal multiplexing.

articleTitle: Ultra-fast clock recovery for burst-mode optical packet communication
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A burst-mode clock recovery circuit design and its module for 10-Gbit/s optical packet communications are presented. A fabricated one-chip module required only 4 ns for clock synchronization. We also describe a burst-mode clock and data recovery experiment at a clock speed of STM64.

articleTitle: Fully electrical 40-Gbit/s TDM system prototype and its application to 160-Gbit/s WDM transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper presents a 40-Gbit/s time-division multiplexing (TDM) system prototype based on InP HEMT digital IC technologies. High-output power photodiode directly drives the digital IC and achieves high-receiver sensitivity. Four-channel 40-Gbit/s wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission is successfully performed.

articleTitle: Improvement of regeneration capabilities in semiconductor optical amplifier-based 3R regenerator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 4-dB reduction of the optical signal-to-noise ratio admissible by an all-optical regenerator is demonstrated. Applied to long-haul transmission, an error-free 10-Gbit/s NRZ transmission over 170,000 is performed with 170-km repeater spacing.

articleTitle: 32/spl times/10 Gb/s distributed Raman amplification transmission with 50-GHz channel spacing in the zero-dispersion region over 640 km of 1.55-/spl mu/m dispersion-shifted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 50-GHz-spaced, 32-channel, 10-Gb/s transmission in the zero-dispersion region over 80/spl times/80 km of 1.55-/spl mu/m dispersion-shifted fiber was successfully conducted by employing distributed Raman amplification. This paper demonstrates a feasibility of dense WDM systems in zero-dispersion region.

articleTitle: 4/spl times/2.5 Gb/s 4.4 km WDM free-space optical link at 1550 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We describe a new world's record for free-space optical communications realized with a 4-channel, 2.5 Gb/s per channel system, operating error-free over a free-space horizontal distance of 4.4 km. This is made possible by three key developments: (1) specialized optical telescope-transceiver terminals, (2) multimode fiber DWDMs and (3) high power 1550 nm Er/Yb optical amplifiers.

articleTitle: Over 200 mW 980 nm pump laser diode module using optimized high-coupling lensed fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The high-power 980-nm pumping laser diode module of 230 mW at kink driving current was fabricated by optimizing the wedge-shape of lensed fiber to achieve 95% coupling efficiency.

articleTitle: WDM optical IP tag switching with packet-rate wavelength conversion and subcarrier multiplexed addressing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We believe we have demonstrated for the first time wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) all-optical IP tag switching with wavelength conversion and subcarrier multiplexed addressing. Switching over four wavelengths covering 16 nm was demonstrated with noninverting wavelength conversion of 2.5 Gbps payloads and burst mode recovery of tag/headers.

articleTitle: Dense wavelength-division multiplexed transmission in "zero-dispersion" DSF by means of hybrid Raman/erbium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Transmission of 25 and 50 equally 100-GHz and 50-GHz spaced 10-Gb/s (OC-192) channels on the ITU grids is demonstrated over eight and four 83.8-km long spans, respectively, of DSF with the zero-dispersion wavelength within the signal wavelength band. Significant performance improvements are obtained with a pump power of only 440 mW with 55-/spl mu/m/sup 2/ dispersion-shifted fibers because of their relatively high Raman efficiency.

articleTitle: Integrated planar waveguide amplifier with 15 dB net gain at 1550 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A packaged Er-doped aluminosilicate planar optical waveguide amplifier (POWA) has shown net gain of 15 dB (22 dB) at 1550 nm (1532 nm) with 150 mW/980 nm pump. Low loss (0.25 dB) mode converters that couple between the POWA and standard P-glass waveguides are also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Bit-rate flexible all-optical clock recovery
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 5 GHz to 20 GHz bit-rate flexible all-optical clock is presented. 10 GHz and 20 GHz pulse trace analysis and 8 Gbit/s to 11 Gbit/s bit-error-rate measurements demonstrate the system qualification. The applied self-pulsating distributed feedback laser is compact, integratable, and requires no RF electronics.

articleTitle: All-optical 2R regeneration at 40 Gbit/s in an SOA-based Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: All-optical 2R regeneration in an SOA-based Mach-Zehnder interferometer is demonstrated at 40 Gbit/s. The regenerative capabilities combined with an input power dynamic range of 16 dB demonstrate the feasibility of this technique at very high bit rates.

articleTitle: Magnetically tunable fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We believe we report the first demonstration of a broad-range (15.7 nm) tuning of fiber Bragg grating using fast, programmable, and latchable magnetic actuation. A key advantage is that the device requires no power except when shifting wavelengths.

articleTitle: A novel switching paradigm for buffer-less WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Optical burst switching (OBS) is proposed to efficiently support IP over wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM). We describe various OBS protocols and in particular, one that can achieve high bandwidth utilization and low blocking probability in bufferless optical networks.

articleTitle: A simple low-cost polymer PLC platform for hybrid integrated transceiver modules
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A polymer planar lightwave circuit (PLC) platform with a simple structure for hybrid integrated optical modules is described and demonstrated. A transceiver module using this low-cost platform has shown high output power (>2 mW at 60 mA) and high responsivity (>0.39 A/W).

articleTitle: Novel temporal/spectral coding technique based on fiber Bragg gratings for fiber optic CDMA application
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel hybrid temporary spectral coding technique based on fiber Bragg gratings for fiber-optic CDMA application is proposed and demonstrated experimentally for the first time to our knowledge. Significant improvement in fiber-optic CDMA networks at high bit rates is expected.

articleTitle: Crosstalk-induced degradation in an optical-noise-limited detection system
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Considering an optical-noise-limited detection system, we established theoretically and experimentally that in-band crosstalk tolerance strongly depends on parameters such as optical signal-to-noise ratio extinction ratio and decision threshold.

articleTitle: Trinal-wavelength-band WDM transmission over dispersion-shifted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Ultrawide-band wavelength-division multiplexing transmission over a dispersion shifted fiber utilizing the 1470-nm band, the 1550-nm band, and the 1590-nm band is demonstrated for the first time to our knowledge.

articleTitle: Photosensitization of optical fiber by UV exposure of hydrogen loaded fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report a photosensitization process in standard hydrogen loaded optical fiber. A persistent photosensitivity is produced by exposure to UV light that can be uniform or spatially tailored along the fiber length.

articleTitle: Photonic spectral encoder/decoder using an arrayed-waveguide grating for coherent optical code division multiplexing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Error-free spectral encoding, 40-km transmission and decoding of 10 Gbit/s, 810 fs, return-to-zero signals are successfully demonstrated using a photonic spectral encoder and decoder pair that uses high resolution arrayed-waveguide gratings and phase filters.

articleTitle: Reliable, high gain-bandwidth product InGaAs/InP avalanche photodiodes for 10 Gb/s receivers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: InGaAs/InP avalanche photodiodes (APDs) with gain-bandwidth products as high as 140 GHz, low effective ionization rate ratio and excellent reliability were fabricated. Receivers using these APDs had sensitivities better than -27.5 dBm.

articleTitle: Novel optical-regenerator using electroabsorption modulators
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Novel optical regenerator architecture employing electroabsorption-modulator-wavelength-converters is proposed. The wavelength converter acts also as a photodiode. The improvement of the Q-factor and the noise reset are experimentally confirmed.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion compensation at 20 Gb/s with a compact distributed equalizer in LiNbO/sub 3/
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: PMD of existing fibers impairs transmission at rates greater than 10 Gb/s. We present a 43 ps PMD compensator in X-cut, /spl gamma/-propagation LiNbO/sub 3/ with cascaded TE-TM converters and demonstrate successful operation at 20 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Spectral phase encoding and decoding using fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a new all-fiber technique for coherent spectral encoding and decoding based on temporal-spectral dispersion and recombination using suitably chirped fiber Bragg gratings. The application potential to optical-code division multiple access telecommunication is discussed.

articleTitle: Tutorial on Protection and Restoration in Optical Networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Equipment supporting dense wavelength-division multiplexing (DWDM) has seen widespread deployment in recent years. With the introduction of wavelength add/drop capability to these systems, coupled with the introduction of optical network elements with “nodal” features-such as optical add/drop multiplexers (OADMs) and optical crossconnects (0XCs)-the ability to add, drop, and in effect construct wavelength-switched and wavelength-routed networks will quickly emerge, as will the often heralded age of Optical Networking. This will present an attractive opportunity to design survivable optical WDM network architectures.

articleTitle: UV-induced absorption, scattering and transition losses in UV side-written fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate that UV-illumination of hydrogen-loaded photosensitive fiber leads to considerable loss. The three contributing loss mechanisms of absorption, scattering, and losses are quantified and discussed.

articleTitle: Intersymbol interference induced by delay ripple in fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have observed the intersymbol interference (ISI) induced on a signal due to traversing a fiber Bragg grating having periodic delay ripple. A simple model of the grating transfer function agrees well with the observed ISI behavior.

articleTitle: Free space optical interconnect at 1.25 Gb/s/channel using adaptive alignment
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Free space optical backplanes have previously required precision mechanics or moving parts. An adaptive alignment technique is described, using redundant VCSEL and detector arrays for real-time mapping of parallel 1.25 Gb/s data channels to aligned links.

articleTitle: Silica-air microstructured fibers: properties and applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present results of three silica-air fiber types possessing unique characteristics, which are not possible with conventional MCVD fibers. We summarize the optical and mechanical properties of these fibers and review potential applications.

articleTitle: WDM optical path-based robust IP backbone network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) optical path-based IP backbone network is proposed as a cost-effective way of realizing robust IP-over-photonic systems. WDM optical paths directly accommodate the IP packets via layer-2 frames.

articleTitle: Fibre non-uniformity caused Bragg grating imperfections
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Variations in the diameter along the length of an optical fiber limits the quality of a grating written into the waveguide. We discuss how fiber design plays an important role in minimizing these imperfections.

articleTitle: Influence of drawing temperature on light scattering properties of single-mode fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Light-scattering measurements on single-mode fibers show that Rayleigh scattering losses are affected very little by drawing temperature change. Drawing-induced losses are explained by an additional contribution: a small angles light-scattering phenomenon.

articleTitle: 1.55 /spl mu/m DFB lasers with integrated spot size converters operating at 2.5 Gbit/s with modulated power over 20 mW for 180 km transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Low-divergence 1.55 /spl mu/m distributed feedback (DFB) lasers with spot-size converter were used to demonstrate <1.5 db penalty after 180 km transmission at a rate of 2.5 Gbit/s with peak power over 20 mW.

articleTitle: System margin enhancement with Raman gain in multi-span WDM transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: With the improvement of 4-dB system margin by distributed Raman gain, we demonstrate error-free transmission of 40 wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) L-band channels with 50-GHz spacing at 10 Gbit/s over 5/spl times/120 km spans of dispersion-shifted fiber.

articleTitle: Multifrequency erbium-doped fiber ring lasers anchored on the ITU frequency grid
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Multifrequency erbium-doped fiber lasers anchored on the ITU frequency grid and using periodic filters are presented. The multifrequency operation is obtained by adding a frequency shifter in the ring cavity.

articleTitle: 765 Gb/s over 2,000 km transmission using C- and L-band erbium doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report 100-channel transmission of both C- and l-band with 765 Gb/s capacity over a distance of 2,000 km. To achieve this transmission result, we utilized dispersion flattened transmission and broadband medium gain erbium doped fiber amplifiers.

articleTitle: Terahertz, zero frequency error, tunable optical comb generator for DWDM applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on the experimental realization of a single comb generator based on phase modulation in an amplified fiber loop, which offers exact referencing to an arbitrary supplied reference frequency and a tunable comb-line spacing.

articleTitle: Widely tunable semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Monolithic widely tunable lasers are reviewed, with emphasis on the grating coupled sampled reflector (GCSR) laser. Methods of controlling the lasers are discussed, leading to wavelength agile integrated wavelength-division multiplexing sources settable to any wavelength within the erbium-doped fiber amplifier window.

articleTitle: 1220 km propagation of 40 Gbit/s single channel RZ data over dispersion managed standard (non-dispersion shifted) fibre
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Error free propagation of a single polarisation optical time division multiplexed 40 Gbit/s dispersion managed pulsed data stream over dispersion (non-shifted) fibre. This distance is twice the previous record at this data rate.

articleTitle: Chaotic lasing effect in a closed cycle in transparent wavelength division multiplexed networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Chaotic lasing effect in a closed cycle of wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) networks with channel power equalizers and gain-damped erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) is observed. It causes degradation in other wavelength channels, but does not saturate the EDFAs.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband WDM transmission using cascaded chirped fiber gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate 32 channel WDM transmission at a per-channel rate of 10 Gb/s over 375 km (five amplified fiber spans) of conventional fiber. Chirped-fiber-grating modules provide dispersion compensation over an 18-nm bandwidth, and a swept-frequency measurement confirms continuous good performance across the entire band.

articleTitle: Investigation of cross-phase modulation limitations on 10 Gbit/s transmission over various types of fiber infrastructures
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We measure the impact of cross phase modulation (XPM) on the transmission performance of a 2/spl times/2 Gbit/s multiplex. In contrast to the other investigated fiber schemes, dispersion-compensated SMF is virtually not affected by XPM down to 50-GHz channel spacing.

articleTitle: CW highly efficient 1.24 /spl mu/m Raman laser based on low-loss phosphosilicate fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the first demonstration of an extremely simple and efficient 1.24 /spl mu/m phosphosilicate fiber-based Raman laser with Bragg gratings written directly in the fiber used. The laser pumped by Nd fiber laser exhibits a slope efficiency of 80%.

articleTitle: Cross-phase modulation distortions in multi-span WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Measurements of the cross talk due to cross phase modulation in a wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) system on conventional single-mode fiber and on nonzero-dispersion-shifted fiber confirm theoretical results on linearity with power and inverse channel spacing.

articleTitle: Effect of spectral-hole burning on multi-channel EDFA gain profile
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We show that a spectral gain profile of a multichannel erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) changes associated with the change in multichannel location, which is well described by a summation of hole burning caused by each signal.

articleTitle: Latency characteristics of wavelength-switched packets in WDM multi-hop ring network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Improvement of the latency characteristic by using a wavelength-tunable laser diode at each node was confirmed through numerical simulations. From these results, the required wavelength switching time was clarified to be <10 ns for 2.5 Gbit/s ATM signals.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s photoreceiver modules comprising InP-OEICs for RZ and NRZ coded TDM system applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 40-Gbit/s photoreceiver modules for 1.55-/spl mu/m TDM system applications covering RZ and NRZ coding are described. The modules contain an InP-OEIC with a monolithic integration of a waveguide-integrated photodiode and a traveling-wave amplifier.

articleTitle: A 2.5 Gbit/s optical ATM cell synchronizer
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An optical cell synchronizer has been implemented to align the phases of incoming optical ATM cells at 2.5 Gbit/s to a reference cell clock. The adjustment ranges is 1 to 511 bits with a precision of 1/4 bit, or 100 ps.

articleTitle: Influence of stimulated Raman scattering on the channel power balance in bidirectional WDM transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The influence of stimulated Raman scattering on the channel power balance in bidirectional wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission has been analyzed experimentally and numerically. Output power levels with 8 channels/direction launched at +10 dBm/ch. differ more than 0.7 dB from linear loss.

articleTitle: Optical layer restoration-an operations perspective
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The deployment of optical layer restoration in large scale networks is examined from the perspective of network operations. Issues addressed include granularity, restoration speed, interworking among network layers, improving reliability and maintainability.

articleTitle: Sub-10 femtosecond timing jitter of a 10-GHz harmonically mode-locked fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present the lowest measurements of timing jitter, to our knowledge, of a harmonically mode-locked fiber laser. Phase detection noise measurements demonstrate a timing jitter of less than 10 fs from 100 Hz to 1 MHz.

articleTitle: Pump induced inhomogeneity of gain spectra in conventional and extended-band EDFAs
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present results on spectral gain changes resulting from small changes of pump wavelength in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs). While conventional-band EDFAs exhibit a significant effect with 980-nm pumping and a smaller effect with 1480 nm, it is absent for extended-band EDFAs operating around 1585 nm.

articleTitle: Athermal silica-based arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) multiplexers with new low loss groove design
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose a new low loss groove design for athermal silica-based arrayed-waveguide grating multiplexers. The insertion loss was 3 dB and the cross talk was -35 dB. The temperature dependence of the channel wavelength change was suppressed to below 0.4 nm in the 0-85/spl deg/C temperature range.

articleTitle: Efficient modelling of holey fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Holey fibers are described using a new technique based on efficient decompositions of the electric field and fiber profile. Unique and interesting dispersion properties are predicted, including dispersion flattening anomalous dispersion below 1.3 microns.

articleTitle: Gain equalization with optimized slanted Bragg grating on adapted fibre for multichannel long-haul submarine transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Slanted Bragg grating and fiber were specially designed for erbium amplifier gain flattening. Results on 11 cascaded 50-km amplified spans show 0.1 dB gain excursion per amplifier on bandwidth as wide as 17.8 nm.

articleTitle: Dispersion properties of photonic bandgap guiding fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We investigate low-index core photonic crystal fibers. Dispersion properties very different from standard fibers are found. Both zero dispersion and very large dispersion is shown possible at 1550 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: All-optical parity checker
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an all-optical digital processing circuit that checks the parity of binary modulated pulse trains. The circuit contains two semiconductor optical amplifier based all-optical switching gates and operates with bit differential optical delays.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s polarization-independent, push-pull InP Mach-Zehnder modulator for all-optical regeneration
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A polarization independent, push-pull InP Mach-Zehnder modulator for 40 Gbit/s all-optical regeneration was implemented. Error-free regenerated transmission over more than 20,000 km is demonstrated. Wavelength independence and immunity to crosstalk is also measured, showing potential for WDM transmission applications.

articleTitle: Line coding for dispersion tolerance and spectral efficiency: duobinary and beyond
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose and analyze a new class of transmission line codes that dramatically increase the dispersion tolerance and spectral efficiency of dense wavelength-division multiplexing transmission. These codes generalize and optimize duobinary signaling, yielding new binary and multibit data representations.

articleTitle: LD and PD array modules assembled in a new plastic package with auto-alignment projections for silicon optical bench
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A plastic package with auto-alignment projections for silicon optical bench was newly developed and four-channel laser diode (LD) and photodiode (PD) array modules assembled in this package are reported.

articleTitle: Stable 200 nm TDM/WDM source based on continuum generation in 2 m of fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: By propagating 500-fs pulses through 2 m of standard fiber followed by 2 m of dispersion-shifted fiber, we generate >200 nm of supercontinuum between 1430 nm and 1630 nm. The supercontinuum is flat to </spl plusmn/0.5 dB over 60 nm and exhibits superior stability and coherence properties.

articleTitle: A low power electroabsorption modulator driver IC for 10 Gbps optical transmitter
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: For 10-Gbps optical transmitter, we have developed a low-power consumption electroabsorption modulator driver IC and observed good characteristics. The power consumption was 0.85 W at a supply voltage of -5 V under the 2.5 Vpp output condition.

articleTitle: The analogy between photonic crystal fibres and step index fibres
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Some properties of photonic crystal fibers quantitatively match those of standard step-index fibers, provided the right analogy is made between them, this is illustrated by calculations of second-mode cutoff (reported here for the first time to our knowledge) and propagation constants.

articleTitle: Integrated real time multi-channel wavelength monitoring circuit using phased-array waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An integrated multichannel wavelength monitoring circuit using specially designed phased-array waveguide grating and detector arrays, which monitors all wavelength-division multiplexing channels in real-time (sixteen channels at 200-GHz spacing), has been demonstrated with /spl sim/0.02 nm accuracy.

articleTitle: New hydrogen aging loss mechanism in the 1400 nm window
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new type of hydrogen aging loss increase of up to 0.21 dB/km at the 1385 nn OH peak can arise in some fibers when exposed to 0.01 atmospheres of hydrogen for less than 4 days at room-temperature.

articleTitle: A novel data format free bit-by-bit quasi-error monitoring method for optical transport network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel data format-free bit-by-bit monitoring method for survivable optical transport networks is proposed. BER evaluation with comparison of BERT and BIP-8 measurement indicates that proposed method has the same capability of SDH/SONET monitoring.

articleTitle: Hierarchical restoration in a backbone network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We describe a cross-connect-based, two-level hierarchical restoration scheme for backbone networks. The scheme offers advantages in requiring less terminating equipment, decreasing the required cross-connect size, and providing a simpler topology for rerouting purposes.

articleTitle: Compact integrated dynamic wavelength equalizer
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An integrated dynamic wavelength equalizer that can control attenuation at 22 points across 35 nm of spectrum in a smooth manner is presented. It achieves low loss and compactness because it consists of a Michelson interferometer with a waveguide grating router in only one arm.

articleTitle: The second and third order dispersion compensation of picosecond pulses achieved by combining two nonlinearly chirped fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We used a combination of nonlinearly chirped fiber Bragg gratings to demonstrate for the first time to our knowledge, second- and third-order dispersion compensation for 1.6-ps and 3.5-ps pulses transmitted over a 66-km-long-shifted fiber around the zero-dispersion wavelength.

articleTitle: Low loss integrated Mach-Zehnder-interferometer-type eight-wavelength multiplexer for 1480 nm band pumping
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate an eight-wavelength PLC-MZI multiplexer to realize high-power 1480-nm band pumping units without using polarization combiners. The fiber-to-fiber insertion loss was lower than 1.2 dB by using laser diodes stabilized by fiber Bragg grating.

articleTitle: A simplified approach to the Bragg grating based Michelson and the in-coupler Bragg grating add-drop multiplexer
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The in-coupler Bragg-grating-based add-drop multiplexer is shown to be identical to a wavelength de-tuned Michelson-Bragg grating interferometer bandpass filter.

articleTitle: Optical CDMA transmission for robust realization of complex and flexible multiple access networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have implemented an optical 8/spl times/155.52 Mbit/s CDMA system with up to 40-km standard fiber, cascaded optical amplifiers, and optical dispersion compensation. The network performance is analyzed for different bit rates and the filter stability requirements are evaluated.

articleTitle: Pulse form reshaping of chirped pulse using optical phase-sensitive amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate the pulse form reshaping of chirped pulses by using the optical phase-dependent gain of an optical phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA). The intersymbol interference between 26-ps-width pulses, introduced by 85-ps/nm dispersion, was successfully reduced.

articleTitle: Fading-free fiber-optic transport of 60 GHz-optical DSB signal by using in-line phase conjugator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Fading-free transport of a 60-GHz optical DSB signal in a 100 km long non-dispersion-shifted single-mode fiber at 1550 nm by inserting a semiconductor optical amplifier phase conjugator in the midway of an optical link is experimentally demonstrated for the first time to our knowledge.

articleTitle: System impairment due to polarization mode dispersion
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A linear model that determines the eye closure due to polarization-mode dispersion is presented. Current 2.5-Gbit/s systems have minor impairment from PMD; however, systems with increased bit rate and/or PMD could suffer from Q-factor fluctuation primarily and reduced average Q-factor.

articleTitle: 270-km 10 Gbit/s WDM dispersion compensation using a chirped AWGM
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We show that a 10-Gbit/s per channel SM-fiber wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) system could be extended from 70 km to 270 km using an array-waveguide multiplexer (AWGM) with a quadratic phase shift added across its waveguide array.

articleTitle: Impact of the polarization mode dispersion on a field demonstration of 40 Gbit/s soliton transmission over 500 km
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 40-Gbit/s single-wavelength alternate polarization soliton field experiment was performed on a dispersion-shifted fiber installed cable 500 km long. Comparison with an equivalent fiber installed in laboratory showed that the main impairment was due to the polarization-mode dispersion.

articleTitle: Integrated phase and magnitude control of a microwave optical subcarrier using a three-contact, vertical-cavity, surface-emitting laser
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new integrated method of phase and magnitude control of a microwave optical subcarrier is demonstrated using a three-contact VCSEL. The entire first quadrant of 16-QAM signal space can be achieved.

articleTitle: Vertical cavity optoelectronic transceivers for short distance data communications links
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel dual-purpose vertical-cavity optoelectronic component, functioning either as a laser or as an avalanche photodetector, is employed in a link as a transceiver unit allowing "ping-pong" communications. Successful system performance is demonstrated at bit rates up to 1.244 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Fiber transmission penalties due to EDFA power transients resulting from fiber nonlinearity and ASE noise in add/drop multiplexed WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We analyze fiber transmission penalties due to erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) power transients that result from fiber nonlinearity and ASE noise in a chain of 10-20 EDFAs with as many as 32 wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) channels. We find due to worst case power transients: (i) system performance is severely degraded (up to few 10s of dB) both in single-mode fiber and dispersion-shifted fiber, (ii) the SNR can be reduced up to 8 dB in a 32-channel system, and (iii) a control channel to suppress power/SNR transients may impose an additional few dBs, which increases with the bit rate.

articleTitle: Cross-talk bandwidth in backward pumped fiber Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report experimental results on Raman gain and crosstalk bandwidth in different backward-pumped fiber Raman amplifiers. Dependence of cross talk on fiber length, fiber loss coefficient and Raman gain saturation is discussed.

articleTitle: Improvement of 1.57-1.61 /spl mu/m band amplification efficiency by recycling wasted backward ASE through the unpumped EDF section
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel structure, which utilizes detrimental backward amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) as a secondary pump source is suggested for a 1.58-/spl mu/m silica-based fiber amplifier. By using the secondary pumping effect from the strong, wasted 1550-nm band ASE power in the unpumped section of the erbium-doped fiber (EDF), it was possible to achieve a considerable improvement in power conversion efficiency, increasing small signal gain by more than 4 dB.

articleTitle: Transmission over 360 km of 110 channels at 2.35 Gb/s from a spectrum-sliced modelocked laser
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the transmission over 360 km of 100 channels at 2.35 Gbit/s from a spectrum-sliced femtosecond fiber laser. Almost all transmitted channels have Q factors >18.34 dB corresponding to error floors below 10/sup -16/.

articleTitle: Wavelength-tunable actively mode-locked fiber ring laser with a Fabry-Perot semiconductor modulator based on carrier-induced refractive index change
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Wavelength-tunable multiple-gigahertz-repetition-rate single- and dual-wavelength nearly-transform-limited short pulses were demonstrated in a mode-locked fiber ring laser using a Fabry-Perot semiconductor laser, which served not only as a mode-locker but also as a wavelength-tunable filter.

articleTitle: Fabrication of vertically coupled glass microring resonator channel dropping filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Air-clad glass microring resonators vertically coupled to buried channel waveguides are fabricated. Channel bandwidths of 3 nm, and free spectral range between 22 to 30 nm are observed for ring radii of 6 to 10 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: Single-wavelength 40 Gb/s soliton field transmission experiments over 400 km fibre without in-line control
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report single-wavelength 40-Gbit/s soliton transmission over 400-km installed fiber lines in Sweden. Both polarization-division multiplexed and parallel solitons were transmitted. The system performance is dominated by the polarization-mode dispersion.

articleTitle: Novel technique for UV-writing of low-loss and high-temperature stable channel waveguides
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Low-loss channel waveguides, stable at over 500/spl deg/C, have been UV written by masking the channel area and exploiting the large negative refractive index changes in germanosilica layers deposited by hollow cathode PECVD.

articleTitle: Poling of UV-written waveguides
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report poling of UV-written silica waveguides. Thermal poling induces an electro-optic coefficient of 0.05 pm/V. We also demonstrate simultaneous UV-writing and UV-poling. No measurable decay in the induced electro-optic effect was detected after nine months.

articleTitle: Feasibility of 1 terabit/s (25 ch/spl times/40 Gbit/s) global-distance, optically regenerated systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The theoretical feasibility of 1 Tbit/s optically regenerated systems over 10,000 km is investigated. The role of key parameters (fiber dispersion slope, mode area, channel and regenerator spacing) on system performance is analyzed.

articleTitle: Wide bandwidth and long distance WDM transmission using highly gain-flattened hybrid amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 1.5-dB gain-flatness over 67 nm is achieved with a novel hybrid amplifier comprising a distributed Raman amplifier pumped at two wavelengths and an erbium-doped fluoride fiber amplifier. Fourteen 2.5-Gbit/s signals spanning 65 nm are successfully transmitted over 900 km using our amplifiers.

articleTitle: Efficient wideband wavelength conversion using cascaded second-order nonlinearities in LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguides
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on wavelength conversion and spectral inversion using cascaded second-order nonlinearity in periodically poled LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguides with an internal conversion efficiency of -8 dB, of more than 50 dB, and bandwidth of 76 nm.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s soliton transmission field experiment over 1,020 km and its extension to 1,360 km using in-line synchronous modulation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the details of a 40-Gbit/s soliton transmission field experiment over 1,020 km, which used a dispersion-compensation technique. The transmission distance was extended to 1,360 km by installing in-line synchronous modulation.

articleTitle: Single material fibres for dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Approximate calculations show that the dispersion of photonic crystal fibers could exceed -2000 ps/nm/km. They could also compensate (to within 0.4%) the dispersion of 35 times their length of standard fiber over a 100-nm range.

articleTitle: Free-space micromachined optical-switching technologies and architectures
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: As wavelength-division multiplexing transmission matures and launches the need for optical networking, free-space micromachined optical switches are emerging as promising candidates for the crossconnects such networks will need. We describe the promise of this new technology and the open questions it raises.

articleTitle: Cross phase modulation resonances in WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a theoretical treatment of cross-phase modulation enhancement due to the effects of periodic gain and loss in an all-optical WDM transmission line.

articleTitle: Wavelength-tunable add/drop filter for optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A wavelength-tunable optical add/drop filter for wavelength-division multiplexing at 1550 nm was realized using planar silicon-oxynitride waveguides. The filters show low insertion loss, high isolation figures and negligible polarization dependence.

articleTitle: Global undersea networks: Technical developments
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Optical technology has led to an amazing increase in the deployment of submarine networks. Each year a new generation is scheduled with a higher capacity; terabit cables are now being planned for service in the year 2000. The paper will present a forecast of the enabling technologies for this booming area.

articleTitle: A new all-fiber bidirectional optical cross-connect with tunable fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new bidirectional optical cross-connect system with tunable fiber Bragg gratings is proposed. It utilizes active bidirectional routers composed of serially connected PZT-actuated fiber Bragg gratings. It is an all-fiber and polarization-insensitive bidirectional optical cross-connect system.

articleTitle: Polymeric optical waveguide with high thermal stability and its application for optical interconnection
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have realized multimode optical waveguides with low loss and high thermal stability by a simple fabrication process using UV-cured epoxy resin, and also proposed useful and low-cost waveguide film devices for optical interconnection.

articleTitle: Suppression of nonlinear waveform distortion using alternate polarization modulation for long distance 10 Gb/s based WDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Alternate polarization modulation has been proposed for long-distance 10-Gbit/s-based wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) transmission systems to suppress SPM-GVD effect. In the 6000-km transmission, the allowable accumulated dispersion, which determines the available WDM bandwidth, was increased by 40% by adopting this scheme.

articleTitle: Cost-merit estimation of introducing optical layer with efficient traffic grooming
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: To quantify the cost merit of introducing an optical layer, we present an estimation of the number of electrical node equipments that can be saved by optical bypassing, using a novel method of computing efficient optical paths configuration.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave optical beamforming network for phased-array antennas employing optical up-conversion and wideband chirped fiber gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel optical beamforming architecture for phased-array antennas operating at millimeter-wave frequencies is presented. Experimental results at 28 GHz have demonstrated very good performance for this technique, based on optical upconversion and wideband chirped fiber gratings.

articleTitle: Fabrication of spectrally clean, long-period grating filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We fabricate spectrally clean long-period gratings in optical fibers. We compensate the measured nonlinear response of the glass to UV light with a computer-controlled exposure schedule. The resulting spectra are free of unwanted harmonic resonances and sidelobes.

articleTitle: Tutorial on WDM System Impairments
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Optical transmission systems with capacity exceeding 100 Gbit/s per fiber are already commercially available. The combined use of high-density wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), high per-channel bit rate and extended-bandwidth optical amplifirs is rapidly pushing the capacity of commercial systems beyond 1 Tbit/s.

articleTitle: The dispersion-OTDR
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have developed an optical time domain reflectometer (OTDR)-like instrument that measures dispersion as a function of distance along fiber spans of up to 50 km, quickly and with great accuracy. Its range is extended to at least 75 km with the use of Raman gain.

articleTitle: DWDM of fiber Bragg grating sensors without sensor spectral dynamic range limitation using CDMA
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate dense-wavelength-division multiplexing (DWDM) of fiber Bragg grating sensors without sensor spectral dynamic range limitation by combining code-division and wavelength-division multiplexing schemes.

articleTitle: A 2.5-Gb/s high-speed PLC module for Gigabit-To-The-Home (GTTH) system
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A PLC module with an avalanche photodiode (APD) and a one-chip receiver IC was developed for use in an ultrabroadband optical access system. The module provides 2.5-Gbit/s downlink capacity and is the fastest PLC module ever reported to our knowledge.

articleTitle: Wavelength selective cross connect using arrayed waveguide lens multi-wavelength filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present an experimental demonstration of a partially equipped 128/spl times/128 OC-192 novel wavelength selective cross connect using a broadcast-and-select architecture. Novel silica multi-wavelength filters are key elements in the cross connect.

articleTitle: Active management of 100-GHz-spaced WDM channels
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate active management of 8 nm/spl times/0.8 nm wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) channels with arbitrary dropping/passing and channel equalization. The optical/add-drop-(de)multiplexing functionality is achieved using a polarization-insensitive spatial-light-modulator-based holographic filter. Finer resolution (50 GHz) and spectral shaping can be straight forwardly attained.

articleTitle: Design of dispersion-managed fiber and its FWM suppression performance
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We describe the design and performance of a dispersion-managed fiber (DMF) whose purpose is to suppress four-wave mixing (FWM) in a wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) system. We fabricated a 40-km-long DMF and confirmed its FWM suppression effects in a 4/spl times/10 Gbit/s WDM experiment.

articleTitle: Polymeric digital optical switch using fluorinated polyimide
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 1/spl times/8 polymeric digital optical switch made using highly reliable fluorinated polyimide has been demonstrated. High-acceleration damp-heat tests show the excellent potential of this switch for use in a nonhermetic package.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated 1.5 /spl mu/m/1.3 /spl mu/m transceiver modules for full-duplex operation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 1.5/1.3 /spl mu/m transceiver-photonic integrated circuits (PICs) with in-line and Y-junction architecture including a 1.3-/spl mu/m wavelength-selective photodetector building block have been fabricated. The characterization of a first Y-junction module in a test bed is presented.

articleTitle: 1.6 Gb/s transmission over 1 km of 62.5 micron-core multimode fiber by subcarrier modulation of 850 nm VCSELs
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the first subcarrier-based optical transmission of 1.6 Gbit/s over 1 km of standard 62.5 micron-core graded index fiber. BPSK, QPSK, and subcarrier-multiplexed BPSK are studied using 850 nm VCSEL sources.

articleTitle: Recent progress of high power laser diodes for EDFA pumping
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We review the state-of-the-art of both 980-nm and 1480-nm lasers for erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) pumping. High coupled power >200 mW as well as high reliability operation can support a dense wavelength-division multiplexed network. We demonstrate high-power EDFA with multipumping length-stabilized pump modules.

articleTitle: Ultra-sensitive optical autocorrelation using two photon absorption
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Autocorrelation of ultrashort pulses using two-photon absorption provides a convenient and sensitive alternative to standard techniques using nonlinear crystals. We review experiments using commercially available laser diodes for ultrasensitive autocorrelation wavelengths around 1.5 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: Architectures for multistage crossconnects
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Numerous issues are involved in the design of a multistage crossconnect. Many of these are concerned with technology and performance. We suggest that network control is a worthy addition to the list of design considerations.

articleTitle: Tunable pulsed fiber-optic parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a tunable optical parametric oscillator that derives gain from a nonlinear fiber Sagnac interferometer pumped by 7.7-ps pulses at 1539 nm. We report a 74-nm-wide tuning range centered on the pump wavelength.

articleTitle: Characteristics of the high-power 980 nm laser diodes with decoupled confinement heterostructure
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Performance of 980-nm high-power InGaAs-AlGaAs laser diodes featuring novel DCH structure is given. A reliability data (50/spl deg/C/70/spl deg/C-300 mW) indicates a potential for telecommunication use. We also achieved 300 mW from fiber module.

articleTitle: Lossless four-channel wavelength selector monolithically integrated on InP
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
