abstract: A four-channel compact wavelength selector with 400-GHz channel spacing has been fabricated by monolithic integration on InP. Lossless operation has been achieved for all channels. Bit-error-rate performance at 2.5 Gbit/s and 10 Gbit/s has also been investigated.

articleTitle: Optical WDM space communications: the next frontier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. I describe the technology and architecture of very high-speed optical space links that will be used in the future as a key building block for global extent satellite-based data networks. With wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) multiplexing of >10 Gbps channels, the cost of these space systems can be very competitive with terrestrial fiber systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic measurements of magnetically-strain tuned FBG for fast reconfigurable add/drop
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We believe we report the first demonstration of a magnetically tunable fiber Bragg grating (FBG) and show a wavelength switching time of 2 ms. The center wavelength is shifted over 4 nm without introducing any discernable amplitude or phase distortion, confirmed by 10-Gbit/s system measurements.

articleTitle: A novel optical device with wide bandwidth wavelength conversion and amplification
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the characteristics of a prototype optical parametric diffuser (OPD), which is a novel optical sampling device. A high conversion efficiency (over -20 dB) was obtained across a wavelength conversion bandwidth of about 83 nm.

articleTitle: 80 Gbit/s transmission over 106 km standard-fiber using optical phase conjugation in a Sagnac-interferometer
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on 80 Gbit/s transmission over 106 km of standard-fiber (D=16 ps/km/nm) using mid-span spectral inversion by four-wave mixing in a semiconductor optical amplifier, which is inserted in a Sagnac-interferometer for CW-pump suppression.

articleTitle: Elimination of crosstalk in the common output amplifier of a multi-wavelength source by gain clamping
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We realized a multiwavelength laser using a hybrid integration technology. Simultaneous laser operation of four wavelength channels could be obtained. To avoid signal cross talk, a novel approach to clamp the gain of the common amplifier is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optimal prechirping for dispersion-managed transmission of return-to-zero pulses
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present analytic expressions that predict the transmission dynamics of chirped return-to-zero (CRZ) pulses in dispersion-managed fibers. The theory enables us to efficiently calculate the prechirping required to optimize system performance.

articleTitle: Performance monitoring in undersea lightwave systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This talk gives an overview of performance monitoring techniques used on today's long haul wavelength-division multiplexing undersea lightwave transmission systems and their applications to tomorrow's terabit undersea systems.

articleTitle: A multihop connection establishment algorithm for all-optical wavelength-routing networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose a heuristic algorithm that can determine the locations of optoelectronic and electro-optic conversions in all-optical wavelength-routing networks, to set up a connection request in a multihop manner if the estimated bit error rate (BER) for the connection is high, so that the signal can be regenerated in some intermediate nodes ensuring a low BER.

articleTitle: Field deployment and evaluation of 1510 nm data communication network for MONET Washington DC network trial
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on the design and field performance evaluation of an embedded, out-of-band, 1510-nm data communication network (DCN) at OC-3c data rate for the eight-wavelength, reconfigurable MONET washington D.C. testbed. The results of this field trial demonstrate that a multinode control and management system can depend on such a highly reliable DCN.

articleTitle: A high-bandwidth optical-pulse-shaping/fiber-optic distribution system for the high-energy OMEGA laser-fusion facility
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A high-bandwidth pulse-shaping/distribution system employing fiber-optic and integrated-optic technology has been built and implemented on the OMEGA laser-fusion facility to deliver variously shaped, 0.1-ns to 5-ns duration, nanojoule optical pulses for amplification and frequency conversion.

articleTitle: Photosensitive Yb-doped double-clad fiber for fiber lasers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Photosensitive at 244 nm double-clad Yb-doped germanosilicate fibers have been developed. Fiber lasers based on these fibers exhibited 65% differential efficiency and 100 mW threshold at both 910 and 980 pump wavelengths.

articleTitle: Bidirectional WDM self-healing ring network based on simple bidirectional add/drop amplifier modules
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a cost-effective bidirectional wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) self-healing ring network using a novel, bidirectional add/drop amplifier module. The restoration time was measured to be <2 ms. The results show that this network could accommodate at least 10 nodes when the node spacing is 80 km.

articleTitle: Tutorial on silicon micromachines for lightwave networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. In my tutorial, I will review what micromachines are, how they are built, and why they will be important to lightwave networks. I will then review work in this area and show examples of modulators, attenuators, switches, active equalizers, add/ drop multiplexers, optical monitors, optical crossconnects, and active component packages that will provide highly functional, low-cost solutions to problems facing the network designers of the future.

articleTitle: Polarization-independent all-optical clock division using a semiconductor-optical-amplifier/grating-filter switch
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate, for the first time to our knowledge, polarization-independent all-optical clock division (CD) of an optical pulse train at 2.88 GHz. This is achieved using a semiconductor-optical amplifier (SOA)/grating-filter switch, where the SOA acts as a spectral shifter by a self-phase modulation (SPM) and the grating filter acts as a spectral shutter. The proposed scheme is very insensitive to the polarization of input pulses and requires very low switching energy (/spl sim/102 fJ). After the all-optical CD operation, we have obtained the output pulse train at 1.44 GHz, which is half the input repetition rate, with high extinction ratio (>20 dB).

articleTitle: A new method to determine the Er-fibre gain coefficient from dynamic gain tilt technique
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new method to determine the Er-fiber gain coefficient is presented using a dynamic gain tilt technique. Results demonstrate that this method is very simple, highly accurate, and especially useful for long-wavelength erbium-doped fiber amplifier.

articleTitle: Tutorial on hybrid fiber coax (HFC) system and network technologies
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Whether rebuilt or newly installed, HFC systems are now evolving from a simple multichannel video broadcasting system to a two-way interactive multimedia network and are becoming an important part of the telecommunication infrastructure worldwide. HFC access technologies involve multidisciplinary engineering fields, including subcarrier multiplexed (SCM) lightwave components and systems, RF modem designs, and medium-access-control (MAC) protocols. This tutorial presents an overview of HFC network services and architectures, lightwave transmissions, and cable modem technologies.

articleTitle: Tapered lattice filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new single-mode, fiber-based lattice filter is described. Filtering is achieved by coupling and interfering the LP01 and LP02 modes at multiple sites. Gain flattening filters are fabricated using only three tapers.

articleTitle: Lithium niobate switch arrays for optical cross-connects
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. The status of lithium niobate guided wave switches and their use in optical crossconnects will be reviewed. The talk will include recent results from the MONET program and a discussion of future applications.

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion mapping by tunable OTDR
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A modified optical time domain reflectometer (OTDR), including a tunable source, is used to measure chromatic dispersion and zero dispersion wavelength along installed fibers with spatial resolution of 100 m. This technique is considerably simpler than the nonlinear ones.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg gratings based multiwavelength cross-connect with high dynamic range
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A reconfigurable multiwavelength crossconnect (MXC) based in fiber Bragg gratings integrated with optical limiting amplifiers is investigated. The MXC has high input dynamic range of over 20 dB. Small power penalty of 0.6 and 1.0 dB for the crossconnect and passing through signal is demonstrated for a 2.5 Gbit/s/spl times/2 100-km system.

articleTitle: Tutorial on Components for Next-Generation High-Speed LAN
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Triggered by the ever-increasing computer speed and the wide application of the Internet, the demand for higher communication bandwidth and interconnectivity is drastically increasing. Networking a group of (computers in proximity to form LAN has become imperative for corporations and organizations to compete and perform.

articleTitle: Negative slope dispersion compensating fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Two types of DC fibers are presented. The first is an improved high figure of merit (267) negative slope dispersion-compensating fiber intended for DC modules. Also presented is a type II DC fiber intended for field deployment that leads to total broadband dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: An optical phase-shift keying direct detection receiver using a high-resolution arrayed-waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An optical phase-shift keying direct detection (PSK-DD) receiver with phase modulation to amplitude modulation conversion using a high-resolution arrayed-waveguide grating is proposed and demonstrated at 10 Gbit/s using an optical PSK-return-to-zero signal.

articleTitle: Picosecond pulse source for OTDM/WDM applications based on arrayed waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 13-wavelength-channel 10-GHz pulse source is demonstrated using a novel scheme incorporating a dispersion-imbalanced fiber loop mirror and an arrayed waveguide grating. The 5-ps-width pulses are of high quality with negligible pedestal.

articleTitle: Over 20 dB of cross talk reduction in an asymmetric bit rate optical transceiver module
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Over 20 dB of crosstalk reduction was achieved by the method, using transmitter bandwidth optimization. With this method, we developed a high-performance optical transceiver module for asymmetric bit rate systems.

articleTitle: Implementing optical noise loading to estimate margin in WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: System margin is determined using a new noise-loading technique in combination with accurate system modeling. For the first time to our knowledge, computation of signal variance is verified by experiments in a 5,000-km multiplexed (WDM) system.

articleTitle: Resonant distortion in vertical cavity surface emitting lasers for RF communication
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present distortion measurements of 850-nm oxide aperture vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) over a 2 GHz to 8 GHz frequency range. A maximum spurious free dynamic range (SFDR) of 107.8 dB-Hz/sup 2/3/ at 2.6 GHz was measured, which we believe is the highest reported SFDR for a VCSEL. Resonant distortion due to the intrinsic nonlinearity of the laser and optical feedback is measured in both free space and multimode fiber-optic links.

articleTitle: Composite-second-order improvement of 15 dB in an optically amplified 110-km AM-VSB CATV transport system using chirped fiber grating
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: To improve system composite-second-order (CSO) of an optically amplified AM-VSB CATV transport system, we investigate the system using chirped fiber grating (CFG) and dispersion-compensating fiber (DCF) separately. We find that the CFG technique is superior to the DCF one in both CSO and carrier-to-noise ratio with satisfied composite-triple-beat performance.

articleTitle: Stimulated Brillouin scattering of the compensating signal in all-optical link-controlled amplifier systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The performance of wavelength-division multiplexed transmission systems using all-optical link control for amplifier gain stabilization can be impaired by stimulated Brillouin scattering of the compensating signal generated from ring but not fiber Bragg grating laser structure.

articleTitle: Hybrid integrated external cavity laser without temperature dependent mode hopping
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose a new integrated external cavity laser, which eliminates temperature-dependent mode hopping by employing silicon between the laser diode (LD) and the grating. Operation without mode hopping is experimentally confirmed from 18/spl deg/C to 34/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Field trial of bidirectional passive optical network employing an EDFA and FM-SCM technique using a 100-km SMF cable installed in a city area
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A bidirectional passive optical network system employing a bidirectional amplifier system was proposed. The system performance was confirmed by the field trial using the 100-km SMF cable installed in the city area for two weeks.

articleTitle: A repeatered regional/WDM local access network for delivery of broadcast digital TV
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have demonstrated the delivery of a digital video service over a repeatered regional/local access network. A single commercial uncooled 1.3-mm distributed feedback transmitter at the head end is capable of serving 2,028 subscribers, with a total distance from head end to host digital terminal (HDT) to subscriber of 46 km. Sensitivity measurements show the wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) PON performance to be within 0.25 dB of the non-repeatered baseline for optical input powers to the HDT of -34 dBm.

articleTitle: Long unrepeatered transmission at 10 Gb/s using adiabatic soliton propagation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate transmission of 10 Gbit/s data over 296 km with no in-line amplification. Adiabatic propagation of picosecond solitons is used to increase the launched optical power and obtain a power budget of >62 dB.

articleTitle: An integrated wavelength locker for waveguide DEMUXes
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A simple technique for precisely monitoring a reference wavelength in order to lock the wavelength channels of a waveguide demultiplexer is proposed and experimentally verified. It incorporates a differential wavelength monolithically integrated on the DEMUX.

articleTitle: Cascaded nonlinearity: a simple technique to compensate Kerr effect in optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have experimentally demonstrated a hybrid optical amplifier comprising a periodically poled LiNbO/sub 3/ crystal and an erbium-doped fiber amplifier. The use of cascaded nonlinearity inside nonlinear crystal made it possible to construct a "nonlinearity-free" optical amplifier.

articleTitle: Adaptive dispersion equalization of 8-ps pulses in 400-km transmission line by monitoring relative phase shift between spacing-fixed WDM signals
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose an adaptive dispersion equalization system based on wavelength tuning and monitoring the relative phase shift between fixed-spacing wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) signals. Adaptive equalization is successfully demonstrated for 40-Gbit/s (8-ps RZ pulses) 400-km transmission.

articleTitle: Fast and widely tunable Bragg grating reflection filter
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A fiber Bragg grating filter device linearly tunable over 45 nm is presented. The device has a maximum tuning speed of 19 nm/ms with a wavelength setting time below 1.5 ms.

articleTitle: Dynamic range comparison of ultrawide-band photonic downconverters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Dynamic range of alternative configurations for a single-channel cascaded-MZM downconverter are compared for the first time to our knowledge. Increased RIN in an optically amplified setup may outweigh increased RF power gain in ultrawideband systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic fiber loop-mirror-filter (LMF) based on pump-induced saturable gain or absorber gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a novel optically tunable, all-fiber narrowband filter based on saturable gain or absorber gratings in a loop mirror. The loop mirror provides built-in interferometric phase alignment between the signal and grating for optimal bandpass or notch MHz to GHz regimes.

articleTitle: 10 Gbit/s asynchronous digital optical regenerator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We believe we describe the first experimental demonstration of an asynchronous digital optical regenerator, which is predicted to be a key component for future high-speed digital optical networks.

articleTitle: Dispersion-managed high-capacity WDM systems using zero-dispersion-flattened transmission line
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The transmission performances of zero-dispersion-flattened transmission line, which consists of standard single-mode fiber and reverse dispersion fiber are described. High-capacity wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission based on 10-Gbit/s signals is demonstrated using the transmission line.

articleTitle: An optical 4-fiber bi-directional line-switched ring
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An optical four-fiber bidirectional line-switched ring is presented. Results from optical protection switching experiments show that restoration in <50 ms is possible. A self-healing, bandwidth efficient, and scalable optical transport network evolving from this architecture is possible.

articleTitle: Quantum cryptography in optical fiber networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Quantum cryptography represents a new paradigm for secure communications in which security is based on fundamental physical laws rather than computational complexity. Recent progress in the development of practical optical fiber-based systems will be described.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion analysis in fibre chromatic dispersion compensators
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Analysis of polarization-mode dispersion in linearly chirped fiber chromatic dispersion compensators has been carried out with several types of fibers. The importance of fiber birefringence as well as fabrication process has been pointed out.

articleTitle: Bi-directional passive optical network for CDMA personal communication service
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a bidirectional passive optical network for CDMA personal communication service. This network could be implemented cost effectively by using Fabry-Perot lasers for the downlink and LEDs for the uplink.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive broadband transparent DCF module with faraday rotator mirror, Raman-amplified by single polarization diode-laser pumping
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A DCF module Raman-amplified by single polarization diode-laser pumping was fabricated. The DCF compensates both dispersion and dispersion slope of 40-km SMF without loss increase from 1530 nm to 1620 nm. The PMD and PDG were 0.01 ps and <0.01 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Error free 80 Gb/s soliton transmission over trans-oceanic (>8,000 km) distances using fast saturable absorbers and dispersion decreasing fibre
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a numerical study of the use of fast saturable absorbers in conjunction with dispersion-decreasing fiber to achieve enhanced transmission of 80 Gbit/s solitons over ultralong distances with an amplifier spacing of 50 km.

articleTitle: Impact of bit pattern and dispersion variation on cross-phase modulation penalty
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Our simulations demonstrate that in wavelength-division multiplexing systems where cross phase modulation is the dominant nonlinear impairment, performance penalties depend weakly on dispersion statistical variations and have a strong bit pattern dependence.

articleTitle: Integrated optical time-division-multiplexer based on planar lightwave circuit
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 80-Gbit/s (20 Gbit/s/spl times/4) optical time-division multiplexing is demonstrated using an optical time-division multiplexer based on a hybrid integrated planar lightwave circuit. Each channel signals independently modulated by mixing in semiconductor optical amplifiers.

articleTitle: Architecture considerations in merging multi-vendor WDM rings for the MONET Washington D.C. network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The architecture of the MONET Washington W.C. area multivendor network resulting from merging wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) rings was analyzed and designed. Connectivity, protection capabilities, and system interoperability were the main considerations for comparison amongst the candidate architectures.

articleTitle: LD-pumped 1.48-/spl mu/m laser based on Yb-doped double-clad fiber and phosphorosilicate-fiber Raman converter
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An all-fiber 1.48-/spl mu/m generator based on a LD-pumped Yb-doped double-clad laser with intracavity Raman wavelength conversion has been developed. Second-order Raman Stokes radiation was generated in a phosphorosilicate-resonator formed by two pair of Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Availability analysis of optical shared protection rings for long haul networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper summarizes the results of availability analysis completed for optical shared protection rings (OSPRs) applied to long-haul networks. Fault scenarios are described for the case of clients with automatic protection switching (APS) although results of the analysis are given for both clients with and without APS. It is shown that for clients with APS, OSPRs can provide avilability comparable to SONET/SDH rings.

articleTitle: Grooming dynamic traffic in unidirectional SONET ring networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We develop circuit assignment algorithms for dynamic traffic in SONET/WDM ring networks. We show that a significant reduction in the number of SONET multiplexers can be achieved by properly allocating SONET add drop multiplexers to nodes.

articleTitle: Method for detecting fiber cuts in a WDM ring with saturated EDFAs
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We compare optical methods for detecting fiber cuts in a wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) ring with in-line erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs). Both simulation and experiment show that differential measurements provide faster and more accurate discrimination than single power measurements.

articleTitle: All-fiber Kerr-based wavelength converter for 1550/1300 nm conversion
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 1550/1300 nm conversion is demonstrated using a novel all-fiber Kerr-based converter. The proposed architecture overcomes the classical interferometer limitations. Walk-off compensation is studied and performed. Simulations and experimentation up to 3 Gbit/s are presented.

articleTitle: Accurate wavelength calibration references for wavelength division multiplexing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have developed transfer standards and high-accuracy internal standards for wavelength calibration in the 1500-nm region. The Standard Reference Material transfer standards are based on the absorption of light by acetylene and hydrogen cyanide.

articleTitle: Microwave phase shifter based on a fibre Bragg grating operating at constant wavelength
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a variable delay line for phased-array antennas based on a fiber Bragg grating of uniform period operating at constant optical wavelength. Time-delay variations of 330 ps in the frequency range 1 GHz to 14 GHz are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Model to predict spectral shape of an hybrid 980 nm-1480 nm pumped erbium doped fibre amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new model for predicting hybrid 980 nm-1480 nm pumped erbium-doped fiber amplified (EDFA) gain spectra, which agrees to better than 0.1 dB with measured results, is presented.

articleTitle: A new linearization approach for modeling timing and amplitude jitter in dispersion-managed optical fiber communications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We developed a new linearization approach to calculate timing and amplitude jitter in systems with arbitrary transmission formats. Our approach yields more precise results than Monte-Carlo simulations at a fraction of the computational cost.

articleTitle: 2.5 Gb/s/spl times/16 channel bidirectional transmission over 560-km of single-mode fiber using bidirectional EDFA based on spectrally interleaved synchronized etalon filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We implemented a bidirectional erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) using two spectrally interleaved synchronized etalon filters. This amplifier was used to demonstrate 2.5 Gbit/s/spl times/16-channel bidirectional wavelength-division multiplexed transmission over re-circulating loop.

articleTitle: Fault surveillance of branched optical networks using an amplifier-generated wavelength-sweeping monitoring source
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a simple and effective fault detection scheme using an amplifier-generated wavelength sweeping source and some fiber Bragg gratings to identify the fiber fault in an optically amplified branched access network without any dedicated monitoring source.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive waveguide DEMUXes with integrated slab polarization compensator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A very simple technique for controlling the inherent birefringence of any planar waveguide demultiplexer, which involves no additional processing and which is effective in any material system, is proposed, modeled, and verified by experiment.

articleTitle: Theoretical prediction and experimental verification of quantum well electroabsorption modulators with bandwidths exceeding 40 GHz
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We experimentally verify the bandwidth and extinction ratio performance of electroabsorption modulators predicted from our simulation. Modulators with bandwidth exceeding 40 GHz for <2 V DC bias have been demonstrated in InGaAsP-InGaAsP multiple quantum wells.

articleTitle: Fiber grating dispersion compensators
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The fabrication technology assessment and system performance of chirped fiber grating dispersion compensators are reviewed with reference to high bit rate advanced wavelength-division multiplexing applications.

articleTitle: Feed-forward LD current controlled fiber optic transmitter and PLL retimed receiver for 622 Mbps and 2.4 Gbps
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel developed fiber-optic transmitter and receiver pairs for 622 Mbps and 2.4 Gbps transmission are presented. They operate over wide temperature range thanks to feed-forward automatic power control (APC) and phase locked loop (PLL) technology.

articleTitle: Active gain equalization for transoceanic WDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose a novel and simple active gain equalization method for transoceanic wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission systems. With this method, the controllable gain tilt after 9000-km transmission was confirmed to be more than /spl plusmn/10 dB over 12-nm signal bandwidth.

articleTitle: Analysis of recovery in radiation-induced loss in rare-earth-doped fibers through master curve/demarcation energy diagrams
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Radiation-induced losses in rare-earth-doped fibers are analyzed in a novel manner. The mastercurve approach is used for analyzing stability of defects induced by radiation. This method can be applied to examine fibers for space applications.

articleTitle: CSO distortions due to the combined effects of self- and external-phase modulations in long-distance 1550 nm AM-CATV systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We found that the combined effect of self- and external phase modulations must be considered in order to precisely predict the CSO distortions in a long-distance 1550-nm externally modulated AM-CATV system, especially when the applied phase modulation index and modulating tone frequency to the integrated phase modulator are high. This result has important implications to the optimum design of 1550-nm transmitter for long-distance AM- and QAM-CATV systems.

articleTitle: Ultra broadband optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Multiple optical amplifier technologies now exist that can be used to provide bandwidths exceeding 40 nm. Performance trade-offs as well as the economics of transmission systems and optical networks will determine the choice among these options.

articleTitle: Isolator-free 2.5 Gb/s, 45 km transmission characteristics in partially corrugated waveguide laser diodes from -40/spl deg/C to 80/spl deg/C under -14 dB external optical feedback
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Using partially corrugated waveguide laser diodes (PC-LDs) with robust and high-yield external optical feedback resistance, isolator-free 2.5-Gbit/s,45-km transmission was demonstrated over a wide temperature range from -40/spl deg/C to +80/spl deg/C under -14 db external optical feedback.

articleTitle: RF gain instability in photonic links due to bias drift in Ti:LiNbO/sub 3/ Mach-Zehnder modulators
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An optimal bias voltage, named the "stabilized quadrature bias voltage," has been identified for Mach-Zehnder modulators, which reduces RF gain instability. A practical remedy for RF gain instability is described.

articleTitle: A novel methodology for measuring coherent homowavelength crosstalk in an optical signal supervisory system
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a novel, easy, and cost-effective methodology that allows an optical signal supervisory system the detection, isolation, and measurement of the coherent homowavelength crosstalk within an optical node. It also identifies the degradation origin.

articleTitle: 16000 km 10 Gbits/sup -1/ soliton transmission over standard fibre by reduction of interactions through optimum amplifier positioning
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We show that by optimizing the amplifier position in a two-stage dispersion map, the (dispersion-managed) soliton-soliton interaction can be reduced, enabling transmission of 10-Gbits/sup -1/ solitons over standard fiber over 16,000 km.

articleTitle: Enhanced sensitivity in WDM optical monitoring using a MARS optical chopper
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A MARS optical chopper is implemented with lock-in detection to enhance the sensitivity of a 1550-nm band wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) optical monitor and improve its immunity of 1/f noise and dc drift. The high chopping rate, 1.02 MHz, it ideally suited for rapid-scanning optical monitors, allowing <100 /spl mu/s filter time constants for high-rate data acquisition.

articleTitle: Reduction of cross-phase-modulation-induced crosstalk by using chirped fiber grating in WDM AM-VSB CATV transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Cross talk induced by cross-phase modulation (XPM) in a 1.55-/spl mu/m WDM CATV transport system can be effectively improved, theoretically and experimentally, from -55.4 dBc to 69.8 dBc by using the chirped fiber grating and polarization control technique.

articleTitle: Cascaded operation of optically gain-clamped erbium-doped fiber amplifiers with equalized gain
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The performance of all-optically gain-clamped, gain-flattened erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) is investigated with the circulating loop experiment. The flat and stable gain is maintained regardless of the number of wavelength channels in the chain of 40 gain-clamped EDFAs.

articleTitle: A 50-Mb/s, ultra-low-power, card-size, 1-V level ONU with battery-backup using one AAA-size cell
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 1-V level operation, 150-mW, 59-cc card-size optical network unit (ONU) with the battery backup time of 5 hrs or more continuous ONU operation from one AAA-size cell, was developed for 50-Mbit/s synchronous transfer mode passive double star (STM-PDS) optical subscriber systems.

articleTitle: Spectral logic gates for byte-wide WDM signal processing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose a new class of all-optical logic gates based on four-wave mixing, designed to operate on multiwavelength input signals. We demonstrate the XOR function with two 2.5-Gbit/s modulated input signals.

articleTitle: 32/spl times/10 Gb/s transmission over 6150 km with a 50 GHz wavelength spacing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The transmission of 32 wavelengths with a 50-GHz spacing and modulated at 10 Gbit/s has been demonstrated over 6150 km. The bit error ratio of the 32 channels is 5.10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Wavelength tracking technique for spectrum-sliced WDM PON
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a simple wavelength-tracking technique that can be used in the spectrum-sliced wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) PON to align the wavelength comb of the waveguide grating router at the central office with the one at the unpowered remote node.

articleTitle: 10 Gbit/s 750 km regenerator-free WDM field trial-upgrading an operated 2.5 Gbit/s based system without changing the installed infrastructure
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A fully managed field-installed wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) link was upgraded with a bidirectional STM-64/OC-192 system and operated with bit error rate <10/sup -13/ without changes of the dispersion-compensated SMF line to demonstrate the upgrade feasibility of transparent links. Dispersion tolerance and PMD influence were investigated.

articleTitle: Suppression of intermodulation distortion in DFB lasers by external optical injection locking
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on the experimental investigation of third-order intermodulation distortion in directly modulated distributed feedback (DFB) lasers under optical injection locking. Nearly 15 dB reduction in third-order intermodulation distortion has been observed from 1.4 to 3.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Error-free propagation of 10 Gb/s wavelength converted RZ data over 20000 km in a dispersion-managed system
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We performed all-optical wavelength conversion of return-to-zero data at 10 Gbit/s using a semiconductor-optical-amplifier/fiber-Bragg-grating hybrid device and propagated the converted data error-free over 20,000 km in a dispersion-managed system.

articleTitle: Soliton sampling for subcarrier multiplexed transmission to eliminate dispersion-induced RF power degradation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate elimination of RF power degradation over 94 km of single-mode fiber in subcarrier transmission from 0.25 to 14 GHz by modulating a 35-ps soliton train. Our results show that solitons are good candidates for subcarrier transmission to avoid degrading dispersion effects.

articleTitle: In-band amplified spontaneous emission noise filtering with a dispersion-imbalanced nonlinear loop mirror
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report removal of in-band amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) noise in a 10-Gbit/s noise-loaded RZ signal using a dispersion-imbalanced loop mirror. The resulting receiver sensitivity is improved from -37.0 dBm to -37.7 dBm. The loop mirror bias dependence of sensitivity is also investigated, and the optimal bias point is found to be where the transmission decreases with increasing input power.

articleTitle: Key functional blocks of optical transport networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summar form only given. This paper will review the latest research achievements in the field of optical routing and switching systems, as well as the related status of enabling technologies for space and wavelength switching, as well as optical regeneration.

articleTitle: Bandwidth controllable filter using the chirped fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrated a novel bandpass filter of which bandwidth can be controlled from 0.1 nm to 2.89 nm using a pair of chirped fiber Bragg gratings and a fiber stretcher based on piezoelectric transducer.

articleTitle: Expectations and challenges in amplifier systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. An intensified competition over the DWDM market has been seen in recent years. Optical amplifier is an important element to minimize the overall system cost. This paper will look into some of the issues and reveal user options for such a system going forward.

articleTitle: All-fibre wavemeter and Fourier-transform spectrometer
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An all-fiber Fourier-transform spectrometer is proposed and demonstrated. The device is simple, compact, and functions as a wavemeter, a network monitor, or a tool for fabrication and testing of very long fiber Bragg gratings.

articleTitle: Novel fiber alignment method using a partially-metal-coated fiber in a silicon V-groove
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose novel fiber alignment method using a partially metal-coated fiber. Rotating the fiber in a silicon V-groove, fiber alignment can be performed. Using this method LD modules obtained a high coupling efficiency (average=-2.72 dB, N=28).

articleTitle: Economic viability of OXC based network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Optical networking seems to be the next major revolution to the telecommunication industry. This paper addresses the key factors involved in embracing this into any operator's network. Various optical networking architecture options are described and economic analyses are shown as the primary filtering method to reduce thousands of variations to a handful of options.

articleTitle: Tutorial on NRZ, RZ, or Solitons: Modulation Format, Your Choice or the Fiber's?
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Since the invention of the erbium fiber amplifier made possible all-optical transmissionover distances significantly longer than the length of spans between electronic regenerators, transmission line designers were confronted with a whole new design space. Parameters like dispersion, self-phase modulation, four-wave mixing, and optical noise (added as a field) became important. In the all-optical transmission line, some modulation formats, for instance FSK and PSK worked poorly, while others, like solitons, which were not appropriate with electronic regenerators, became possible.

articleTitle: Single-end continuous-wave polarization mode dispersion measurement in long single-mode fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Single-end measurement of statistical properties of polarization mode dispersion parameters was carried out by means of a continuous wave scheme based on the analysis of the Fresnel reflection at fiber far-end.

articleTitle: Nonlinear crosstalk and SBS reduction by carrier suppression in an analog WDM optical communication system
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Nonlinear cross talk and stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) reduction are demonstrated in an analog wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) optical communication system using optical carrier suppression. Cross talk reduction by 20 dB over 2 GHz is achieved. SBS is negligible without employing any frequency or phase dithering.

articleTitle: Practical benefits of 4-fibre WDM rings with realistic traffic
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Channel provisioning in four-fiber wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) rings is studied for realistic telecom-operator traffic. For static traffic, wavelength conversion is of no benefit. For dynamic traffic, especially with churn, 1+1 protected WDM rings may, surprisingly offer higher capacities. For both cases we present the most suitable wavelength assignment algorithms.

articleTitle: Impact of polarization hole burning effect in transoceanic wavelength division multiplexed systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have investigated the impact of polarization hole burning effect in transoceanic wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) systems experimentally. A polarization scrambler should be indispensable in transmission for wide channel separation.

articleTitle: Accumulation of transient power excursions in WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We study transient power excursions of an all-optically gain-controlled amplifier chain. We observe that the speed of residual power excursions increase much faster with the of amplifiers than uncontrolled networks.

articleTitle: Directly modulated 2.5 Gb/s/spl times/16-channel WDM transmission over 640-km of single mode fiber using dispersion compensating fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a directly modulated 2.5 Gbit/s/spl times/16-channel wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission system over 640-km of single-mode fiber using DCF. The capacity of this system was increased to 130 Gbit/s by replacing twelve directly modulated 2.5-Gbit/s channels with externally modulated 10-Gbit/s channels.

articleTitle: ATM-PON FTTH access networks and services
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper describes a deployment scenario for optical access networks and ATM services using the ATM-PON systems. A new ATM bearer service with guaranteed frame rate (GFR) and a future issue in dynamic bandwidth allocation for the ATM-PON were also presented. The ATM-PON system is an economical high-speed optical access system which provides universal access networks for multimedia services.

articleTitle: Collisions in dispersion managed soliton propagation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We study collisions in dispersion-managed pulse propagation at and near zero net dispersion. We show that the collisions can lead to group velocity changes and spectral collapse. Filters prevent spectral collapse but do not affect the velocity changes.

articleTitle: A new signal processing technique for interferometric fiber-optic sensors
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new signal processing technique using a frequency modulated semiconductor laser maintains high accuracy even using inexpensive multimode Fabry-Perot lasers. The application of this technique is reported in temperature measurement with a fiber Fabry-Perot sensing head.

articleTitle: OLCR characterization of long period grating induced cladding modes
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The group index of well-defined cladding modes has been characterized for the first time to our knowledge by optical low-coherence reflectometry (OLCR) with a precision <10/sup -4/. Very good agreement between theoretical and experimental results has been obtained.

articleTitle: Dispersion compensation using only fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We are able to perform dispersion compensation using a chirped fiber grating without a circulator by placing three gratings in series and utilizing the ability of gratings to couple to cladding modes.

articleTitle: Profile-controlled long-period fiber gratings based on periodic microbends
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a high-performance long-period grating based on arc-induced microbends. Filter profile control is realized by simple apodization technique.

articleTitle: Increase of crosstalk penalty due to nonlinear propagation in optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Simulations show that nonlinear propagation can increase system impairments originated by linear cross talk in optical nodes. In a conventional fiber link, system penalties were measured at crosstalk levels about -8 dB lower than in linear conditions.

articleTitle: A view of next generation optical communication systems-possible future high-capacity transport implementations
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Possible implementations of next-generation high-capacity transport are presented and associated technical challenges are discussed. From the spectral efficiency of conventional modulation formats, and based on substantial system integration experience, it is estimated that a practical capacity for a single 1000 km fiber is between 2 and 5 Tbit/s, assuming a 10 THz transmission window.

articleTitle: Reliability of fluoride fiber module for optical amplifier use
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have investigated the reliability of a fluoride fiber module with a hermetically sealed package for practical optical fiber amplifier use. We confirm that our module has long-term stability under practical environmental conditions and sufficient mechanical strength.

articleTitle: Grating-assisted Mach-Zehnder OADM using cladding-photosensitive fibre for cladding mode suppression
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the realization and performances of an OADM using a grating-assisted Mach-Zehnder interferometer made of cladding-photosensitive fiber. This component provides low-cladding-mode coupling (<0.6 dB for 36 dB apodized grating isolation) and a high return loss up to 30 dB.

articleTitle: Improved transmission of chirped signal from semiconductor devices by pulse reshaping using a fiber Bragg grating filter
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Spectral filtering of chirped signals with an edge of a fiber grating filter improves propagation in nondispersion-shifted fiber the improvement is due to a temporal shift of the frequency modulation with respect to the amplitude modulation.

articleTitle: Dy/sup 3+/-doped Ge-Ga-S-KBr (or CsBr) glasses for the 1.3 /spl mu/m fiber amplifier materials
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The addition of CsBr and KBr in Ge-Ga-S glasses doped with Dy/sup 3+/ showed a remarkable increase in the 1.32 /spl mu/m emission intensity. Lifetimes and quantum efficiency also increased to 700 /spl mu/s and 100%, respectively compared to 38 /spl mu/s and 17% usually found in Ce-Ga-S glasses.

articleTitle: Fiber based acousto-optic filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Reviews recent progress in the development of all-fiber acousto-optic tunable filters that are of increasing interest for their applications in wavelength-division multiplexing systems. Active gain flattening of erbium-doped fiber amplifiers will be described in detail.

articleTitle: 20 Gb/s transmission of dispersion-managed solitons over 20,000 km
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have propagated 20-Gbit/s data over 20,000 km without any observed pulse-to-pulse interaction achieving an error rate <1/spl times/10/sup -9/ in a dispersion-managed soliton system.

articleTitle: Wide range of operating conditions for a 1000 km-2.5 Gb/s transmission with a new WDM optimized design of integrated laser-electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) optimized design of integrated electroabsorption modulator distributed feedback lasers provides a great tolerance on operating conditions and laser wavelength: 2.5 gbit/s transmission over 1000 km is performed for /spl Delta/I/sub laser/=70 mA, /spl Delta/T/sub chip/=20/spl deg/C, and /spl Delta//spl lambda//sub laser/=10 nm.

articleTitle: High speed and high gain-bandwidth-product resonant-cavity InGaAs/InAlAs avalanche photodiodes
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An AlInAs/InGaAs resonant-cavity SACM avalanche photodiode with high external quantum efficiency (/spl sim/70%),low noise (k<0.3), a unity-gain bandwidth of 24 GHz, and a gain-bandwidth-product of 290 GHz is reported.

articleTitle: AWG-DMUX transmission characteristics improvement using grating lattice filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Synthesis methods of grating lattice filters (GLFs) with poles and zeros are derived. AWG-DMUX cross talk is improved drastically by using GLF with shaper filter characteristics and small size.

articleTitle: Ultra high speed soliton transmission in the presence of polarization mode dispersion using in-line synchronous modulation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: It is shown numerically that in-line synchronous modulation is especially useful for extending the transmission distance in the presence of large polarization-mode dispersion in ultra-highspeed (40 and 80 Gbit/s) optical soliton transmission systems.

articleTitle: Broadband access over HFC networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: In the light of providing broadband services, this paper will discuss three issues: value: why hybrid coaxial fibre (HFC)?; technology: what we can do?; choice: and where to go next?.

articleTitle: SMF 300 km transmission experiment by using a newly developed 10 Gbit/s lightwave transceiver with an electro-absorption modulator integrated LD
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 10-Gbit/s lightwave transceiver with an EA/LD module has been newly developed to meet the STM-64 interface. The back-to-back receiver sensitivity of -16.8 dBm and SMP-300 km amplified transmission experiment with the power penalty of 0.6 dB have been successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Monolithic integration of distributed balanced photodetectors for high performance RF photonic links
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on the microwave performance of a novel velocity-matched distributed balanced photodetector. A 30-dB rejection of the common mode signals and a 17-dB suppression of the laser relative intensity noise have been achieved.

articleTitle: Data-format-free 622-Mbit/s/ch 12-channel parallel optical transmitter and receiver
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A data-format-free 622-Mbit/s/ch 12-channel optical transmitter and receiver have been developed. They provide a skewless PECL interface parallel link for 100-m transmission operating in the ambient temperature range from 0-70/spl deg/C with a 3.3 V power supply.

articleTitle: 320 Gbit/s WDM transmission over 450 km of LEAF/sup R/ optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate transmission of 32/spl times/10 Gbit/s over 450 km of LEAF/sup R/ fiber with BER /spl sim/10/sup -13/, using the same dispersion compensation for all channels. The large effective area fiber strongly reduces all nonlinear effects, limiting the fiber-induced penalty to <1.3 dB.

articleTitle: Novel 1.55 /spl mu/m VCSELs with top metamorphic GaAs/GaAlAs and bottom InP/InGaAsP Bragg reflectors
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel 1.55-/spl mu/m surface-emitting laser structure based on a tunnel junction for current injection and GaAs-AlAs top mirror directly grown on InP cavity in a 2 in. compatible process allows cw operation at room temperature.

articleTitle: High isolation balanced photonic microwave mixers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An integrated photonic microwave mixer, implemented with cascaded balanced bridge Mach-Zehnder modulators, is presented. The input and local oscillator frequency components are effectively rejected at the output, as demonstrated using a lithium niobate device.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of highly tolerable dispersion-managed soliton system designed for trans-oceanic distance transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Large system margins were successfully achieved in dispersion-managed soliton transmission experiments over 10,000 km at 10 Gbit/s and 20 Gbit/s with 53-km repeater spacing. Optimum system parameters were easily designed by considering pulse spacing and dispersion compensation period as primary parameters.

articleTitle: A programmable rate detector for rapid-reconfigurable rate-transparent optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report a programmable, rapid-response bit-rate detection and selection circuit that can handle a discrete and continuous range of data rates from 10 Mb/s to 1.3 Gb/s for programming burst mode and conventional clock data regeneration (CDR) functions.

articleTitle: Bandpass filter transfer characteristic of a complex-apodized arrayed-waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We determine a bandpass filter equivalent transfer function for a complex-apodized arrayed-waveguide grating. A combined near-parabolic phase-profile with e/sup -1/ Gaussian amplitude-truncation produces both a trapezoidal passband and 10 ps group delay over a 12-nm passband.

articleTitle: Noise optimisation of polarisation independent wavelength converters based on dual-pump four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We analyze the noise issues of polarization-independent four-wave mixers based on dual-orthogonally polarized pumps. Noise optimization is demonstrated for the first time to our knowledge in such devices at 10 Gbit/s giving a >5 dB improvement.

articleTitle: Seamless 32/spl times/10 Gb/s transmission over 320 km of 1.55 /spl mu/m dispersion-shifted fiber using wavelengths ranging from 1546 nm to 1587 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper demonstrates 32/spl times/10 Gbit/s transmission over 1.55 /spl mu/m dispersion-shifted fiber. The channels are seamlessly allocated from 1546 nm to 1587 nm. Wideband optical amplifiers employing distributed Raman amplification are used as in-line amplifiers.

articleTitle: Ultra high reliability, ultra high power 1480 nm pump laser diodes
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: High-performance extremely reliable 1480-nm pump laser diodes have been developed. High facet powers for low drive currents (220 mW at 500 mA), narrow far field (22/spl times/17/spl deg/) and long median life (>1/spl times/10/sup 8/ hours) are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Considerations on optical wavelength multiplexing versus optical time multiplexing in transport network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We compare optical wavelength multiplexing and time multiplexing techniques for optical transport network by studying the space switch sizes of optical cross connects (OXCs) and their interfaces as a function of the fraction of add/drop traffic.

articleTitle: Push-pull fused vertical coupler switch
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A single electrode, push-pull fused vertical coupler (FVC) switch using macroscopic crystal inversion symmetry is demonstrated. The anisotropic linear electrooptic effect in a zinc-blende crystal is used to achieve optical switching under 12 V reverse bias for a 6.9-mm-long FVC.

articleTitle: Applying undersea technologies to Project Oxygen
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Project Oxygen is a visionary network, which win be constructed in phases and connect more than 50 countries with up to 160,000 km of new undersea fiber-optic cable. The network will integrate the newest and most sophisticated technologies for providing ubiquitous end-to-end customer telecommunications services. In this paper we review these technologies and their application to Project Oxygen.

articleTitle: Wireline and wireless access networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Numerous technical and competitive forces are driving the redefinition of access networks around the world, but technology choices and economic challenges create a complex maze of options. We review the driving forces, issues, and technologies involved, drawing specific comparison between wireless (fixed and mobile) and wireline alternatives.

articleTitle: Wide bandwidth high capacity systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: In recent years, advances in wide-bandwidth optical amplifiers have led to significant progress in high-capacity, multiwavelength communication systems. These developments will be instrumental in enhancing the capacity and functionality of future lightwave networks.

articleTitle: Photonic network research activities and testbed experiments in NTT
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This presentation will discuss the basic concept of the future photonic network. Recent advances in photonic network technology development will be addressed and the testbed experiments that will be conducted starting in 1999 will be reviewed.

articleTitle: 4/spl times/40 Gb/s, 75-km WDM transmission over conventional fiber using a broadband fiber grating
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate four-channel wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission over conventional fiber at per-channel rate of 40 Gbit/s. A 6-nm-bandwidth chirped fiber grating is used for dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Waveguide-grating-router lasers for WDM
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Waveguide-grating-router lasers are multiwavelength lasers consisting of an array of semiconductor optical amplifiers integrated with a waveguide grating router. These devices can provide accurately spaced wavelengths that are inherently stable and can be simultaneously or fast-switched between.

articleTitle: Results of the PHOTON and MOON field trials
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The PHOTON and MOON projects prove the feasibility of all-optical networking by implementing field trial networks in Europe, demonstrating repeaterless 10-Gbit/s transmission over more than 1000 km within an eight-channel wavelength-division multiplexing grid, optical cross-connecting and management of a photonic network with three optical crossconnects and line amplifiers.

articleTitle: OC-48/STS-48c IP direct on wavelength application
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Synchronization, protection, restoration, and architecture are described for a direct on wavelength IP application. Interfaces for direct connection to dense wavelength-division multiplexing equipment are defined and experimental results for a 20,000-km transmission experiment are presented.
