articleTitle: New multimode fiber ribbon for parallel optical interconnection
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: For parallel optical transmission, the new-type multimode fiber ribbon with very low skew has been developed. Its skew is 0.50 ps/m. Further, it has been found that the fiber ribbon has stable skew characteristics against the external stress.

articleTitle: Tutorial on High-Capacity Optical Transmission System Design
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. The tutorial will focus on design rules for high-speed optical transmission systems. An overview of technologies used today to overcome system impairments such as nonuniform amplifier gain and chromatic dispersion will be presented. Also being presented is a review of some of the future technologies required to overcome today’s technical hurdles and allow for further advancement in transmission capacity. In addition, there will be a discussion of design tools that the future system designer will need.

articleTitle: Control monitoring of routing bits and data packets in WDM networks using wavelength-to-time mapping
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a wavelength-to-time technique for control monitoring in a wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) network. We recover the routing header bits across parallel wavelength as well as determine the existence of data packets for switching purposes. We show results for a routing-bit monitor of multiple channels with the speed of 2.5 Gbps and a packet/frame monitor for multiple channels with the speed of 100 MHz.

articleTitle: Dispersion managed RZ propagation in a circulating loop with NZ-DSF and DCF with 100 km EDFA spacing and dispersion period
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Nonlinear propagation is reported for dispersion-managed 10 Gbps RZ data patterns in the net anomalous-, zero-, and normal-dispersion regimes. The maximum error-free distance achieved without controls is 8800 km with 100-km erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) spacing.

articleTitle: Technologies for hundreds of Gb/s capacities in undersea lightwave systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The technologies to realize hundreds of Gbit/s capacities in transoceanic distance systems are discussed in this paper. The effectiveness of the periodic dispersion slope compensation and the reduced dispersion slope fiber is reviewed.

articleTitle: Photonics R&D programme in Germany-results of selected projects
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. "Photonics" has been one of the main R&D programmes in information technology conducted by the German government. In April 1998, its second four-year-phase was concluded, resulting in the development of advanced technologies for broadband optical fiber systems.

articleTitle: Micromachined optical crossconnects with integrated signal-monitoring functionality
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a single-chip optical-crossconnect module with integrated signal-monitoring functions for fast mesh-network restoration. High speed photodetectors are integrated in hybrid form with free-space micromechanical structures to achieve good performance and connection-monitoring, potentially in a compact low-cost configuration.

articleTitle: Optical communications research in European community programmes
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper discusses the future directions and important changes for European Community research in optical communications, in the context of future research programmes (1999-2003), and the success and achievements of previous programmes (1994-1998).

articleTitle: Experimenting optical solutions for building and home networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Low-cost optical components for building and home networks are discussed. Implementations of optical links into existing copper-based systems demonstrate that fiber-based solutions can be easily integrated at an affordable cost.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a highly scalable 100-Gbps OTDM computer interconnect with rapid inter-channel switching capability
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present an experimental demonstration of an error-free 100-Gbps OTDM broadcast star multiprocessor interconnect. A highly scalable novel node design provides interchannel switching speed on the order of the single-channel bit period (1.6 ns).

articleTitle: 1.24 Gb/s, 40 km optical code division multiplexing transmission by using spectral bipolar coding of broadband incoherent light
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Error-free 1.24 Gb/s OCDM transmission over 40 km by using spectral bipolar coding of broadband incoherent light has been demonstrated for the first time. The proposed system using broadband incoherent light source will simplify the system design and enhance the flexibility of future optical networks.

articleTitle: Analytical model describing transients within a gain-clamped erbium-doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present an analytical model suitable for investigation of transient effects within a gain-clamped erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) experiencing a change to the input signal or pump power. We test the validity of assumptions made and discuss the limitations of the model presented.

articleTitle: Demonstration of sequential 100 Gb/s word TDM packet add/drop functionality using a looped-back configuration
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We show sequential 100-Gbit/s packet processing by looping an all-optical packet add/drop multiplexer on itself. The packets from two different sources are routed with 17-dB contrast ratio and demultiplexed with 20-dB contrast ratio.

articleTitle: A primary-referenced frequency stabilisation technique for use in highly dense wavelength division multiplexing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a technique for the frequency stabilization of a bank of channel lasers to produce a primary-referenced 25-GHz frequency comb. Channel stability and are better than 5% of the channel spacing.

articleTitle: Grating writing through the fibre coating using a 248 nm excimer laser
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Fiber Bragg gratings have been written through the fiber coating using a 248-nm excimer laser for the first time to our knowledge. A standard off-the-shelf coating was used, and 92% reflectivity gratings were obtained with an index change of 2.4/spl times/10/sup -4/.

articleTitle: High capacity EDFA with output power to support densely loaded channels
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: High-channel capacity is demonstrated with a 36-nm gain-flattened erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) with over 28 dBm output power. Wavelength-multiplexed and Raman-based pump sources are used to achieve the high output maintaining telecom grade reliability.

articleTitle: Low-cost compact WDM components for LAN applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. Short-distance (100 m-10 km) data links will soon require bandwidths of 10 Gbaud and higher. Half-inch-wide wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) transceiver modules, for both multimode and single-mode fiber, may be the most likely solution. Low-cost component technologies necessary for fully integrated modules will be discussed and results presented.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable soliton transmission using periodic dispersion compensated normal dispersion fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We investigated numerically nonlinear RZ-pulse transmission through periodic dispersion-compensated normal dispersion fiber, and find that ultrastable transmission mode exists in this situation. This mode indicates better characteristics than the lines using anomalous dispersion fibers.

articleTitle: Specialty optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Within the past decade, several fiber-based devices have achieved significant commercial success, including fiber lasers, amplifiers, filters, sensors, and gyroscopes. This discussion considers the development fibers that enable these devices.

articleTitle: Dual cavity optical automatic gain control for EDFAs
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We believe we report the first demonstration of dual-cavity optical automatic gain control (OAGC). The dual-cavity technique results in improved stability of the amplifier gain spectrum under pump and signal power variations as compared to conventional OAGC.

articleTitle: Array waveguide grating routers for 50 GHz applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Current performances and future prospects of arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) demultiplexers with 50-GHz channel spacing are described. Cross talks of <-30 dB are obtained in 40-ch 50-GHz spacing AWGs. A 16/spl times/16 AWG router with <-37 dB cross talk is also described for a future N/spl times/N interconnection systems.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive static strain fiber-Bragg grating sensor using an interrogating laser locked to stable atomic lines
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Atomic absorption lines provide stable optical frequency references, which can be used to interrogate strain-induced frequency shifts of fiber Bragg gratings. High sensitivity of 1.2 nanostrain//spl radic/Hz at 1.5 Hz is obtained using this novel technique.

articleTitle: Gate arrays using gain-clamped semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Gate arrays using gain-clamped semiconductor optical amplifiers have been successfully implemented in optical cross-connects for wavelength-division multiplexing routing applications as well as in fast optical packet switching experiments. Recent achievements on these devices will be reviewed.

articleTitle: An optically-efficient RF modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Our RF modulator uses a novel arrangement of two low-biased Mach-Zehnder modulators within a ring laser, eliminating resonances and improving efficiency by over 7 dB relative to an externally modulated configuration. This will be useful for DC power-limited analog photonic links.

articleTitle: Measurement of the nonlinear response in a strongly pumped erbium doped amplifiers for all-optical switching
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Measurements of the decay time of real-time gratings in highly doped erbium fiber and analysis of the nonlinear response are presented. For strong pumping conditions the response for a nonlinear optical switch can be 50 /spl mu/s.

articleTitle: Efficient and low-noise operation in a gain-flattened 1580 nm band EDFA
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The power conversion efficiency of 35% and the noise figure of 5.1 dB are obtained in the 1580-nm band erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) composed of the first stage backward pumped at 980 nm and the second stage backward pumped at 1480 nm.

articleTitle: Accelerated measurement of low BERs in fiber optic communication systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. We report the results of an experiment designed to quantify the relationship between an offset in the decision threshold of a high-speed optical receiver and the bit-error performance of the system.

articleTitle: The performance of a 10 Gbits/s filtered dispersion-managed soliton system with lumped amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We simulated the performance of a 10-Gbit/s filtered dispersion-managed soliton system using Monte-Carlo techniques. The predicted noise behavior was in excellent agreement with the measured data.

articleTitle: Improvement of fs/ps pulse shaper by miniaturization and use of enhanced filter bandwidth
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A micro-optical fs pulse shaper is presented conceptually and experimentally; the 50-nm filter bandwidth gives improved pulse shape at acceptable pulse extension. Moreover, an integrated optical ps pulse shaper is proposed with inherent aberration compensation.

articleTitle: 1560- to 1610-/spl mu/m wavelength EA-modulator integrated DFB-LDs for extended-band 2.5-Gb/s/ch and 10-Gb/s/ch WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We developed EA-modulator integrated DFB-LDs covering 1.56-/spl mu/m to 1.61-/spl mu/m wavelengths on a single wafer, and tested them in long-distance transmission experiments for the first time to our knowledge. Transmissions at 2.5 Gbit/s over 600 km and 10 Gbit/s over 500-ps/nm dispersion were successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: High-coupling-efficiency aspheric microoptics integrated on a Si-V groove for a high-speed MiniDIL transmitter
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Highly efficient microoptics mounted on a Si-V-groove in a 4.5-mm-high MiniDIL has been developed for use in a high-speed, long-haul transmitter. The optics consists of a 1.5-mm-diameter 0.55-NA aplanatic aspheric singlet and a 2-mm-diameter microisolator. The coupling from a laser diode to a single mode fiber was 67% in the fiber alignment area of /spl plusmn/275 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: Trimming of center wavelength of ARROW-type add/drop filter by UV irradiation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A vertical coupler filter with a polysilane cover layer is fabricated for the trimming of the center wavelength of the filter by UV irradiation. A wide trimming range of 59 nm is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable polarization independent all-optical demultiplexer using four wave mixing in a dispersion shifted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel polarization-independent all-optical demultiplexer using four-wave mixing in a dispersion-shifted fiber is demonstrated employing a 4/spl times/10 Gbit/s optical time-division multiplexing transmitter. The polarization dependency is lower than 0.5 dB and no bit-error-rate floor is present down to 10/sup -13/.

articleTitle: Ultra low noise long wavelength EDFA with 3.6 dB external noise figure
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A long-wavelength erbium-doped fiber amplifier (LW-EDFB) is reported showing a near-quantum-limited external noise figure as low as 3.6 dB. The amplifier configuration uses a buried optical filter and optical isolator to achieve this performance.

articleTitle: 16 WDM optical packet routing experiment over 640 km transmission distance at data rate of 2.5 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate 1024 byte, 16 wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) optical packet transmission experiments including a wavelength routing function over 640-km transmission distance at the data rate of 2.5 Gbit/s. The bit error rate (BER) after 640 km transmission is 10-11 with no BER floor.

articleTitle: Efficient approach to estimate collision-induced timing jitter in dispersion-managed WDM RZ systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We developed an approach that allows us to create an efficient numerical algorithm that accurately estimates collision-induced timing jitter in wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) RZ systems. The computational time is reduced by two orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Low-loss channelized WDM spectral equalizer using lightwave micromachines and autonomous power regulation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 16-channel 100-GHz spacing WDM spectral equalizer having athermal grating multiplexer/demultiplexers and MEMS variable attenuators was demonstrated with <9.1 dB excess loss, >50 dB dynamic range and autonomous power regulation using self-powered optical limiters incorporating InGaAs photogenerators.

articleTitle: High power side-pumped Er/Yb doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A high-power Er/Yb double-cladding fiber amplifier, side-pumped through a V-groove by a 100-/spl mu/m-wide broad stripe laser diode exhibited 32 dBm output power, 57 dB small signal gain, a 3 dB gain compression at 28 dBm, and a 15% electrical to optical power conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Sampled nonlinearly-chirped fiber-Bragg-grating for the tunable dispersion compensation of many WDM channels simultaneously
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have fabricated and characterized a tunable dispersion compensator that utilizes a specially designed sampled nonlinearly-chirped fiber Bragg grating (FBG), which is suitable for wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) channels. The dispersion can be tuned from 200 to -1200 ps/nm. We experimentally demonstrated tunable dispersion compensation using the sampled nonlinearly chirped FBG in a 10-Gbit/s WDM system. All three channels achieve BER=10/sup -9/ after both 60 km and 120 km of SMF by tuning the dispersion of the grating between -550 and -1100 ps/nm.

articleTitle: -31 dBm sensitivity of a monolithic transmit-receive-device over wide temperature range
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: High system performances (-31 dBm), over wide temperature range, were demonstrated by a monolithic in-line transmit-receive-device, designed for single fibre, bi-directional transmission in full-duplex operation at 155 Mbit/s.

articleTitle: Accumulation of jitter in cascaded wavelength converters based on semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Timing jitter accumulated by cascading wavelength converters is investigated. A trade-off between minimum jitter and a high extinction ratio is identified. We predict that 20 converters cascaded at 10 Gbit/s yields <20 ps of jitter and an extinction ratio >9.6 dB.

articleTitle: 10 GHz mode-locked ring laser with external optical modulation of a semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a novel technique for short pulse generation, based on the externally induced fast saturation of a semiconductor optical amplifier. We demonstrate a 11-ps, 10-GHz fiber ring laser source.

articleTitle: Crosstalk due to optical fiber nonlinearity in WDM CATV lightwave systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Cross talk in a two-wavelength 1550-nm system at subcarrier frequencies 50 MHz to 800 MHz is investigated. Its dependence on subcarrier frequency, wavelength spacing, and optical power is measured. At wavelength spacings >4 nm, gain from stimulated Raman scattering accounts for most of the cross talk.

articleTitle: Wavelength standards and stabilization for WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The optical frequency drift allowed against the channel spacing was estimated for WDM system design. Our multiwavelength simultaneous monitoring circuit holds the frequency drift within a few giga-herz. This drift range is sufficient to realize the WDM systems that offer the spectrum efficiency of 0.2. We also demonstrated an accurate optical frequency comb generator anchored at 193.1000 THz as a secondary optical frequency standard.

articleTitle: A novel method of removing optical fiber coating with hot air stream
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We discuss a new non-contact technique of removing optical fiber coating in a continuous and uninterrupted manner with hot air stream. The mean breaking stripped optical fiber tensile strength was 4.5 GPa.

articleTitle: All-fiber bandpass filter with adjustable transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A polarization-insensitive (/spl plusmn/0.1 dB) all-fiber bandpass filter with 2-nm bandwidth and >25 dB suppression of nonresonant light uses a pair of long-period gratings and a core block. Filter transmission is adjustable over a 20-dB range.

articleTitle: Optical regional access network (ORAN) project
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The DARPA-sponsored ORAN project is an architectural study of economically providing broadband wavelength-division multiplexing access to high-end users. The ORAN architecture is a scalable, flexible, cost-effective access network that delivers both huge bandwidth and high degree of upgradability.

articleTitle: Temperature-sensitive long-period fiber gratings for wideband tunable filters
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present a new type of long-period fiber gratings with enhanced temperature sensitivity of 80 nm/100/spl deg/C via the use of specially designed polymer. New structures are presented, which should enable tunable filters for communications systems.

articleTitle: Codoping effects in fibers for active applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The influence of codopants on the optical and thermal properties of ytterbium- and neodymium-doped fibers for high-power applications was investigated concerning absorption, spectral and time-dependent fluorescence, loss, crystallization behaviour and diffusion interplay of the dopants.

articleTitle: Dynamic erbium-doped fiber amplifier with automatic gain flattening
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate, for the first time to our knowledge, a dynamic EDFA based on automatic active gain flattening. Wide-dynamic-range gain/power control is achieved with <0.6 dB signal ripple over 30 nm in various operating conditions. We also show a significant advantage of the dynamic EDFA over conventional one in cascaded structures.

articleTitle: An electrochromic variable optical attenuator (ECVOA)
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: New electronically controlled infrared variable optical attenuators based on thin film electrochromic technology are presented. Initial ECVOA prototypes have up to 15 dB attenuation range, 0.5 dB insertion loss, and a switching rate of 5 dB/sec. These devices are broadband, continuously variable, compact and polarization insensitive.

articleTitle: 1-Tb/s (40-Gb/s/spl times/25 ch) WDM transmission experiment over 342 km of TrueWave(R) (non-zero dispersion) fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We have demonstrated a successful, error-free 1-Tb/s transmission experiment over 342 km of TrueWave(R) fiber using 40 Gb/s OTDM (optical time-division multiplexing) transmitter and 3R receiver. Fiber chromatic dispersion was effectively compensated for using negative-slope dispersion compensating fiber.

articleTitle: Multi-carrier and m-QAM modulation based on integrated single side band lightwave source
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: System experiments of a fully integrated millimetric single-side-band lightwave source are reported. Complex modulation schemes (64 QAM) are transmitted on 38-GHz carrier with very clear constellation and good bit error rate. Four-carrier transmission is also demonstrated with low penalty.

articleTitle: Simultaneous multi-channel conversion of analog and digital signals by polarization independent difference-frequency-generation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a polarization-independent simultaneous conversion of two optical wavelength channels carrying four-channel subcarrier-multiplexed FM-analog video channels and an optical datagram with a 2.5-Gbit/s data payload and a 155-Mbit/s header.

articleTitle: 500 Gb/s (50/spl times/10 Gb/s) WDM transmission over 4000 km using broadband EDFAs and low dispersion slope fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 500 Gb/s, over 4000 km transmission was moderated with 22 nm-bandwidth EDFAs and low dispersion slope fiber. By reducing the dispersion slope and fiber nonlinearity, the transmission distance was almost doubled compared to the previous experiments with similar capacity.

articleTitle: Very high speed driver and photoreceiver modules for 40 Gbit/s optical communications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Driver and photoreceiver modules, suitable for 40 Gbit/s, are presented based on a GaAs P-HEMT technology. The driver exhibits an 18-dB gain over 41-GHz bandwidth and outputs 3 Vpp in 50 ohms; the photoreceiver exhibits a 10.4 pA/VHz input noise over 28 GHz and a 65-dB ohm transimpedance gain over 37 GHz.

articleTitle: Towards uniform channel performance in dynamic WDM systems and networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Several channel-degrading effects are present in dynamic reconfigurable wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) systems and networks. These effects must be addressed by tunable methods so that signals do not fade with time. The relevant issues to be addressed include; dispersion compensation, power equalization, PMD compensation, and EDFA gain flattening and transient control.

articleTitle: Large-scale demonstration of multi-wavelength optical networking in MONET Washington DC network
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. This talk will describe plans and progress towards the deployment of a multiwavelength optical networking testbed in Washington D.C. by the Multiwavelength Networking Program (MONET) Consortium.

articleTitle: Field trial experiment of CDMA fiber-optic microcellular system: FoMiCell
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report on the field trial experiment of a bi-directional passive optical network for CDMA microcellular systems. This network is useful not only for implementing cost-effective microcellular systems but also for covering the radio-blind areas such as underground shopping malls.

articleTitle: Spectral response apodization of Bragg-like optical filters with a novel grating chirp design
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel grating chirp design providing symmetric apodization without perturbing local propagation constants is successfully applied to realize codirectional grating assisted filter. This technique is suited for apodization of Bragg grating filters and mirror spectra as well.

articleTitle: Free-space micromachined optical crossconnects: routes to enhanced port-count and reduced loss
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We investigate fundamental loss mechanisms in free-space micromachined optical crossconnects due to diffraction, aperturing, and mirror-curvature, and identify means of combating them. The effects are shown experimentally to permit 16/spl times/16 crossconnects with 2.9 dB of loss. Theory suggests a route to 1024-port multistage switches with 6 dB of loss.

articleTitle: Toward realizing a tera-bit per second throughput photonic transport system for bandwidth abundant multimedia communication
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The 320-Gbit/s pre-prototype photonic system throughput is categorized by an upper set of parameters. In order to realize the anticipated number of WDM channels, tera-bit per second throughput capability is demanded. We show an architecture that promises wavelength expandability. It is based on an 8/spl times/8 delivery and coupling type optical switch, and can be expanded in units of 8 wavelengths. The wavelength multiplexing level can be increased to 32, if demanded. The large-scale photonic transport system requires a larger ON/OFF ratio in routing switches and smaller crosstalk in wavelength-demultiplexers.

articleTitle: Toward terabit/s single-channel transmission
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The considerable challenge of terabit/s single-channel optical transmission using a femtosecond pulse train is presented. Recent improvements in input pulse quality and a walk-off free dispersion-flattened nonlinear loop mirror for demultiplexing are described.

articleTitle: High-birefringence nonlinearly-chirped fiber Bragg grating for tunable compensation of polarization mode dispersion
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a tunable polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) compensator using a high-birefringence nonlinearly chirped fiber Bragg grating (HN-FBG). Our device is capable of generating a 100 ps to 320 ps time delay between the polarization axes and tunable over 2.3 nm. For a 10-Gbit/s signal, we show that 170-ps tunability is realized by stretching the HN-FBG.

articleTitle: Effect of molecular water on thermal stability of gratings in hydrogen-loaded optical fibers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Photolytically generated water causes induced loss at 1.55 /spl mu/m as well as decay of fiber gratings in UV-irradiated hydrogen-loaded fibers at temperatures below 350/spl deg/C. These side effects can be eliminated by annealing at 500/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Service-specific recovery of wavelength connections in WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We investigate the recovery of wavelength-shifted and wavelength-continuous connections in a multiservice wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) network, where different services are simultaneously affected by a failure. As the basic performance measures, we use restorability, blocking probability, and efficiency of wavelength utilization.

articleTitle: Optical path monitoring based on the identification of optical cross-connect input ports
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a new optical path monitoring method based on the identification of optical crossconnect input ports. This simple method has the scalability for the number of nodes and wavelengths in the network.

articleTitle: New fiber-optic microwave filters with complete tunability and reconfiguration properties using a linearly chirped fiber grating feeded by a laser array
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a new family of fiber-optic microwave filter that provides full tunability and fast transfer function reconfiguration using a laser array signal, and a linearly chirped fiber grating.

articleTitle: C-band to L-band shift of 80 mn (10 THz) using four-wave mixing in a semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We present the first demonstration of an 80-nm wavelength shift by four-wave mixing from the C-band to the L-band. The power penalty at 10/sup -9/ BER for a 2.5 Gb/s signal is less than 1.0 dB.

articleTitle: Broadband dispersion compensating module considering its attenuation spectrum behaviour for WDM system
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Dispersion-compensating module capable of flattening the dispersion spectrum in 80 km of single mode fibre (SMF) was successfully developed while realizing attenuation variance within 0.35 dB/module in 1530 nm to 1570 nm and attenuation fluctuation <0.1 dB/module in -5/spl deg/C to 50/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: 30 Gbit/s operation of a traveling-wave electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Electroabsorption modulators with traveling-wave electrodes have been designed and fabricated using MOCVD grown InGaAsP-InGaAsP quantum wells. 30-Gbit/s transmission was demonstrated with a 2-/spl mu/m-wide 300-/spl mu/m-long device.

articleTitle: First undersea-qualified 980 nm pump laser diode module evaluated with massive life test
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 980 nm pump laser diode modules with a failure rate as low as 30 FIT for 27 years lifetime have been successfully developed. These are the first undersea-qualified 980 nm pump sources and are to be used in upcoming transoceanic submarine systems.

articleTitle: Positive and negative thermal poling of germanosilicate fibres
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: In situ measurements of thermal poling of germanosilicate fibers under positive and negative poling voltages show different dynamics of a linear electro-optic effect induced into fibers. The mechanism for the induced electro-optic effect is addressed.

articleTitle: 20 Gbit/s all-optical regeneration and wavelength conversion using SOA based interferometers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A novel optical translator that can perform 3R-regeneration and wavelength conversion of high-speed return-to-zero signals is demonstrated at 20 Gbit/s. Efficient retiming and bit-error-rate performance is measured using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with integrated semiconductor optical amplifiers.

articleTitle: Comparison of the cascadability of conventional and gain-clamped semiconductor optical amplifier gates in multi wavelength optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A detailed investigation of the cascadability of gain-clamped semiconductor optical amplifiers (GC-SOAs) and SOAs in wavelength-division multiplexing networks is presented. The analysis shows far superior cascadability of GC-SOAs at a channel bit rate of 2.5 Gbit/s in systems with up to at least 16 channels.

articleTitle: 23 dBm output power Er/Yb co-doped fiber amplifier for WDM signals in the 1575-1605 nm wavelength region
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report, for the first time to our knowledge, theoretical and experimental results concerning a broadband and gain-flattened Er,Yb-codoped double-cladding-fiber amplifier, which provides up to 23-dBm output power in the wavelength region 1575 nm to 1605 nm.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s transmission over 186.6 km of installed fibre using mid-span spectral inversion for dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Transmission of 40-Gbit/s data over 186.6 km of installed standard fiber has been demonstrated for the first time to our knowledge using phase conjugation by four-wave mixing in a semiconductor opitcal amplifier (SOA) for dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: 80 Gbit/s single wavelength OTDM soliton transmission over 172 km installed fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Single wavelength soliton transmission at 80 Gbit/s has successfully been performed over 172 km installed fiber. Soliton data with pulse widths of 4.5 ps was transmitted with an average power penalty for all eight time-division-multiplexed channels of 1.3 dB.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s field test on an installed fiber link with high PMD and investigation of differential group delay impact on the transmission performance
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 40-Gbit/s OTDM transmission over a field-installed dispersion-compensated 130-km single mode fibre (SMF) link was demonstrated successfully (BER < 10/sup -12/). The impact of high PMD (7.8 ps) in the order of the RZ pulse width (7 ps) was studied in detail.

articleTitle: Transient effects in wavelength add-drop multiplexer chains
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical study of the transient power fluctuations of wavelength add-drop multiplexer chains caused by the dynamic interaction of servo-controlled attenuators and saturated erbium-doped fiber amplifiers. The mechanisms responsible for this oscillatory behavior are identified and remedies are proposed.

articleTitle: Single sideband modulation techniques and applications
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Techniques to generate optical single-sideband modulation with and without carrier are presented. Various applications are reviewed including combating dispersion effects, RF frequency translation, and grating characterization.

articleTitle: Realization of high power and wavelength stabilized 980 nm-pump laser diode module with Fiber-Bragg-Grating by optimizing the effective reflectivity with Spatial-Hole-Burning effect
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Effective reflectivity of fiber Bragg grating (FBG)-locked 980-nm laser module was analyzed relating to spatial hole burning. The optimized external-cavity design realized wavelength fluctuation under /spl plusmn/0.3 nm. Power degradation by FBG was below 10%. End-of-life guaranteed power exceeded 150 mW@250 mA/spl sim/300 mA.

articleTitle: Fiber-to-the-home/desktop using Ethernet
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose, demonstrate, and characterize a novel, passive fiber-to-the-home/desktop system using Ethernet protocols and low-cost commercially available Ethernet and fiber-optic components.

articleTitle: 11 Gb/sec data transmission through 100 m of perfluorinated graded-index polymer optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report for the first time data transmission at 11 Gb/sec through 100 m of low loss (33 dB/km) perfluorinated graded index plastic optical fiber using inexpensive, uncooled, unisolated, Fabry Perot lasers at 1.3 /spl mu/m and a simple InGaAs pin photodetector.

articleTitle: 340 Gb/s (34*10 Gb/s, 50 GHz spacing DWDM) straight line transmission over 6380 km with full system implementation assessment
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the first demonstration of 340 Gb/s, 50 GHz DWDM straight-line transmission over 6380 km with performance fully consistent with transatlantic plant installation.

articleTitle: Modeling vs. experiments of 16/spl times/10 Gbit/s WDM chirped RZ pulse transmission over 7500 km
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate a good agreement between experiments and simulations on a 16/spl times/10 Gbit/s wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission system over 7500 km with an average Q-factor >16 dB. We used a simulation technique based on careful evaluation of the key physical effects that produce system impairments.

articleTitle: Internal connectivity of optical crossconnects in opaque networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The impact of the internal OXC connectivity on the network cost is investigated. As a result, full connectivity inside the OXC is not required for realistic cost scenarios of optical switches.

articleTitle: Thermally stable gratings in optical fibers without temperature annealing
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Uniform UV light exposure of a fiber substantially increases the thermal stability of its Bragg grating. Both grating writing and thermal stabilization can now be performed without stripping the fiber coating.

articleTitle: Protection of a priority connection from an optical switch failure in mesh networks with planar topologies
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A new methodology is presented for protecting a priority connection through a failed switch in mesh optical networks with planar topologies. The proposed technique, which is based on line-switching, is fast, distributed, and autonomous.

articleTitle: A novel bi-directional add/drop module for single fiber bi-directional self-healing wavelength division multiplexed ring networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose and demonstrate experimentally a novel bidirectional add/drop module by using two waveguide grating routers and fiber gratings. The results conform its feasibility for the development of single fiber bidirectional self-healing wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) ring networks.

articleTitle: All-optical packet header recognition and switching in a reconfigurable network using fiber Bragg gratings for time-to-wavelength mapping and decoding
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable all-optical header recognition and routing of a 2.5-Gbit/s packet stream using time-to-wavelength mapping with a fiber Bragg grating array correlation decoding. We achieve penalty-free routing using a 1.6-ns guard time. This technique would be useful to enable high-speed all-optical packet switching nodes.

articleTitle: Component technologies for DWDM demultiplexers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper reviews state-of-the art dense wavelength-division multiplexing demultiplexers (DWDM) for commercial deployment in high-capacity optical networks. Fiber-optic component technologies, features, designs, and performance are compared for various network applications.

articleTitle: Ultra-low loss, temperature-insensitive 16-channel 100-GHz dense wavelength division multiplexers based on cascaded all-fiber unbalanced Mach-Zehnder structure
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 16-channel, 100-GHz spacing dense wavelength-division multiplexer was fabricated using a cascaded all-fiber unbalanced Mach-Zehnder structure. This device demonstrates the lowest insertion loss (1.2 dB) reported to date and exquisite channel uniformity. By using a passive compensation technique, the center wavelength also exhibits a low temperature dependency (<2 pm//spl deg/C).

articleTitle: Upgrading SONET rings with WDM instead of TDM: an economic analysis
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We compare a time-division multiplexed (TDM) upgrade of a legacy SONET ring to a single higher speed ring, versus a wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) upgrade path, in which it is possible to retain the legacy ring and add additional "virtual rings" at different wavelengths and lower speeds. The paper makes the case that the WDM option can be economically compelling.

articleTitle: 160 Gbit/s optical sampling by a novel ultra-broadband switch based on four-wave mixing in a semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate 160 Gbit/s all-optical sampling by a compact, ultra-broadband, and low noise switch based on four-wave mixing. The switch combines high contrast (>25 dB), high linearity (>20 dB), and high temporal resolution (1.7 ps).

articleTitle: Comparison between optical fiber birefringence induced by stress-anisotropy and geometric deformation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A variational formulation based vector perturbation model is used to compare the contribution of stress anisotropy and geometric deformation towards optical fiber birefringence. We show that stress impacts the step-index type profiles more than the typical dispersion-shifted type profiles.

articleTitle: Electro-absorption modulated 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength selectable DFB array using hybrid integration
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time an EA-modulated hybrid integrated wavelength selectable laser comprised of 1.55 /spl mu/m DFB laser array and amplifier/modulator chips fabricated using a novel spot-size converter integration technique, and optically connected via silica-on-silicon waveguides. The device operates at 2.5 Gbit's over 16 50 GHz spaced channels with SMSR>33 dB, peak power from +1.6 to -6.2 dBm, and r.f. extinction ratio >0.39 dB for 2.6 V/sub p-p/ drive.

articleTitle: Integrated all-active Mach-Zehnder wavelength converter with record signal sensitivity and large dynamic range at 10 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: An optimized all-active Mach-Zehnder wavelength converter is presented. At 10 Gbit/s, a conversion penalty below 1 dB can be maintained for input signal powers as low as -10 dBm. The signal power dynamic range is at least 15 dB.

articleTitle: A 10-Gb/s optical asynchronous cell/packet receiver with a fast bit-synchronization circuit
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A 10-Gbit/s optical asynchronous cell-packet receiver with a fast bit-synchronization circuit has been developed for achieving beyond Tbit/s optical switch. Less than nine-bit fast acquisition time and <1.5 dB receiver sensitivity penalty have been achieved.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a 10,000-channel, 200-Gbit/s throughput WDM/SCM broadcast-and-select system for local networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We successfully test the feasibility of a 10,000-channel (32 wavelengths with 310 subcarriers), 20-Mbit/s/channel (200-Gbit/s throughput) wavelength-division multiplexing and subcarrier-multiplexing broadcast-and-select system over a 20-km optical fiber.

articleTitle: Hybrid and monolithic integrated optic/millimeter-wave converters for 60 GHz radio-over-fiber systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Hybrid as well as monolithic integrated /spl lambda/=1.55 /spl mu/m optic/millimeter-wave converters were developed and investigated experimentally based on detailed microwave simulations. Both converters working near 60 GHz showed responsitivities of about 1 A/W in good agreement with the simulations.

articleTitle: All-optical regeneration and wavelength conversion in an integrated semiconductor optical amplifier/distributed feedback laser
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Simultaneous all-optical regeneration and wavelength conversion is demonstrated for the first time to our knowledge in a laser-based device. After 95 km of fiber, a negative sensitivity penalty of -1.3 dB is achieved for conversion from 1548 nm to 1553.5 nm.

articleTitle: Field trial of OAM-signal transport capabilities with a 10 Mchip/s LED-direct sequence spread spectrum system suited for OAM-signal-transport in transparent optical WDM-networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A direct sequence spread spectrum (DSSS) transmission system with LED-transmitter suited for OAM-signal transport in transparent optical wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) networks has been built and successfully tested with a four-channel WDM link over 1511-km distance.

articleTitle: Capacity allocation using WDM in fiber-wireless access networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper discusses the impact of fixed and flexible wavelength routing in fiber-wireless access networks. Based on the capacity required, an optimal location is identified for the dynamic wavelength.

articleTitle: Impact of the dispersion map on long-haul 40 Gbit/s single-channel soliton transmission with periodic dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The impact of the dispersion map on 10-Gbit/s single-channel transmission was experimentally investigated. The transmission performance was significantly varied with the dispersion map. By using the optimum dispersion map, 40-Gbit/s transmission over 10,200 km has been achieved.

articleTitle: Photon statistics of NRZ signals in a high-bit-rate optically pre-amplified direct detection receiver
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We verify experimentally, over a dynamic range of 58 dB in the probability distribution, that the preamplified laser light in a lightwave receiver, rather than being Gaussian distributed, is noncentral-negative-binomial distributed.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive nonlinear optical loop mirror demultiplexer using twisted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We reduce the polarization sensitivity of a nonlinear optical loop mirror from 5 dB to 0.5 dB by twisting fiber at 8 turns/m. Twisted fiber equates the nonlinear phase-shift terms of the parallel and orthogonal polarizations.

articleTitle: Full 40 Gbit/s OTDM to WDM conversion: simultaneous four channel 40:10 Gbit/s all-optical demultiplexing and wavelength conversion to individual wavelengths
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: 40 Gbit/s signals are simultaneously all-optically demultiplexed and wavelength converted into four 10 Gbit/s channels of individual wavelengths with a penalty below 1.5 dB,using only one monolithically integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer with semiconductor optical amplifiers.

articleTitle: Dispersion and crosstalk of optical minimum-phase filters in wavelength division multiplexed systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The amplitude and phase responses of optical minimum-phase filters are uniquely related to each other and therefore their cross talk and dispersion characteristics cannot be adjusted independently. The implications for wavelength-division multiplexed (WDM) systems will be shown experimentally and analytically.

articleTitle: SuperNet and NGI
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The talk will cover the DARPA's role and areas of investment in the Next Generation Internet Program. Examples of individual projects will be highlighted.

articleTitle: Erbium/ytterbium-codoped glass waveguide laser producing 170 mW of output power at 1540 nm
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: This paper describes the fabrication and performance of an ion-exchanged, channel waveguide laser in erbium/ytterbium-codoped phosphate glass, which has produced 170 mW of cw power near 1540 nm.

articleTitle: Investigation of stimulated Raman scattering limitation on WDM transmission over various types of fiber infrastructures
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We measure the impact of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) on the power distribution of a 32-channel multiplex after 100 km transmission over various fiber types. The effects of fiber loss, fiber length and channel number increase are also characterized.

articleTitle: Protection strategy and management of WDM optical path transport networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: To construct the future multimedia backbone network, wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) optical path networks that support various transport protocols are required. This paper proposes an effective network protection strategy and management technologies for such networks.

articleTitle: Impact of higher-order polarisation mode dispersion on a 10 Gb/s system over installed non-dispersion shifted fibre
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report experimental results demonstrating that the variation in system performance due to second-order polarization-mode-dispersion effects can be decreased through a reduction of the net chirp.

articleTitle: Measurements of cross-phase modulation induced crosstalk in an L-band EDFA
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We measure the cross talk due to cross phase modulation in an L-band erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA). The effect is larger than the one seen in C-band amplifiers and becomes the dominant effect in some wavelength-division multiplexing systems.

articleTitle: Main results of the ACTS OPEN France-Belgium field trial
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Results of the ACTS OPEN France-Belgium are reported. Wavelength-division multiplexing transmission and routing performance has been investigated. Especially, bit-error-rate measurements out in various network configurations.

articleTitle: Affordable fibre access network for developing countries
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: In the near future, more telephones are likely to be provided using fiber access network in India than anywhere else. This paper presents why this is happening and describes the access solution of operator's choice.

articleTitle: Tutorial on Fundamental Limitations of EDFAs in Amplified Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Summary form only given. This tutorial outlines various factors in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) causing fundamental limitations in lightwave transmission systems, linear propagation being primarily assumed. It is divided in two parts. In the first, we recall definitions for spectral inversion and gain, noise figure, SNR and Q-factor, as related to optical amplifier chains; saturation-induced effects on EDFA bandwidth are also considered. The second part is concerned by practical limitations in bandwidth, noise figure and output power, and related technologies enabling their minimization (gain equalization, multiple-stagehybrid pumping, glass hosts).

articleTitle: Opto-electronic and all-optical wavelength translators and their cascadability
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate superior cascadability performance of bit-rate transparent all-optical interferometric wavelength translators compared to optoelectronic translators. For a translator bandwidth of /spl sim/2 times the bit rate, 9 optoelectronic and 75 all-optical translators can be cascaded.

articleTitle: Continuously tunable high power fiber lasers with 11 nm tunability
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A tunable interactive fiber laser is analyzed and experimentally demonstrated with high single-frequency output power exceeding 62 mW and 11.2 nm continuous tuning. The fiber laser has a low relative intensity noise <-165 dB/Hz and excellent environmental stabilities.

articleTitle: A simple monitoring technique for WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a simple technique that could be used to monitor the wavelengths and optical powers of wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) signals simultaneously by using fast Fourier transform with pilot tones and a fixed Fabry-Perot etalon filter.

articleTitle: The behavior of silica optical fibers exposed to very high-pressure hydrogen environments
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We placed silica optical fibers into hydrogen environments of up to 30,000 psi (2,041 atm) and characterized their photosensitivity, mechanical strength, and H/sub 2/ diffusion rate and solubility. UV-induced index changes in the fibers were >10/sup -2/.

articleTitle: Low drive voltage, 40 GHz LiNbO/sub 3/ modulators
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Frequency-dependent drive voltage is reported in velocity-matched, packaged, LiNbO/sub 3/ interferometers with and without etched ridges. V/sub /spl pi//'s of 7-7.5 V at 40 GHz are demonstrated, with the etched ridge device showing a 1/2-1 V advantage.

articleTitle: 1.4 W saturated output power from a fibre Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: Fiber Raman amplifiers with high output power and a 50% net pump to signal conversion efficiency are reported. A 100-nm supercontinuum based upon a 10-GHz, 8-ps pulse source was generated strong nonlinear interaction in the amplifier.

articleTitle: AWG based device for a WDM/PON overlay in the 1.5 /spl mu/m fiber transmission window
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We propose a special arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) configuration for an overlay of wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) channels on a number of distributed broadcast channels. The new approach offers potential for realization of a compact device for a WDM/PON upgrade.

articleTitle: Direct single-mode fiber to free space coupling assisted by a cladding mode
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We demonstrate initial experiments that verify the feasibility of cladding-mode assisted fiber to free-space beam coupling based on a long-period fiber grating combined with a phase-adjusting core region at the fiber tip.

articleTitle: All-fiber add-drop multiplexer using a tilted fiber Bragg grating and mode-selective couplers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We describe an all-fiber add-drop multiplexer constructed with readily available components: a tilted fiber Bragg grating in a two-mode fiber and mode-selective directional couplers. The simple configuration allows the implementation of standard fiber Bragg grating technologies for improved performance.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of dispersion management for an 8/spl times/10 Gbit/s WDM transmission over non-zero dispersion shifted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate that an 8/spl times/10 Gbit/s wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) transmission with 200-GHz channel spacing over nonzero-dispersion-shifted fiber requires dispersion management when using field channel powers. This is then investigated and optimized.

articleTitle: Role of the Q factor estimation in the field trial of 10 Gbit/s transmission at 1300 nm with semiconductor optical amplifiers between Madrid and Merida (460 km)
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We compare different methods for the evaluation of the Q factor in optical transmission systems when strong patterning effects are present. The results have been applied to investigate the performance of the Madrid-Merida operation link.

articleTitle: Thermally tunable polymer Bragg grating OADMs
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: We report the fabrication of tunable Bragg grating optical add/drop multiplexers (OADMs) in polymers. They exhibit 45 dB reflection with strong sidelobe suppression and no cladding-mode coupling, and they are thermally tunable at a rate of -0.256 nm//spl deg/C.

articleTitle: A multi-port add/drop router using UV-induced gratings in planar waveguides
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: A low-loss, reconfigurable add/drop multiplexer that can route channels between two fibers is presented. Hitless switching is demonstrated on a two-channel device with signals and switching times <500 /spl mu/s.

articleTitle: The proper definition of noise figure of optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC/IOOC . Technical Digest. Optical Fiber Communication Conference, 1999, and the International Conference on Integrated Optics and Optical Fiber Communication
abstract: The noise figure definition currently in use for the characterization of optical amplifiers is criticised. Its shown that it is inconsistent with the IEEE standard established for electronic amplifiers. A noise figure definition is proposed that is consistent with the IEEE standard and that is shown to be superior to the one currently in use.
